2326578623.name: Fortunate Star
2326578623.flavor: When it shines at dusk, luck will surely come your way.

586671776.name: Something New
586671776.lore:
"Do you ever tire of the work?" asks Eva Levante.

Banshee-44 looks up from his workbench. Eva often crosses in front of his kiosk on her walks to and from the Bazaar, striking up conversations with him in passing when she does. He briefly wonders if they've had this particular talk before; he wouldn't put it past her to simply let it play out to spare him the embarrassment of not remembering it.

"Can't say that I do," Banshee replies cordially. "Memory's not so great. Every gun feels like a new one."

Eva nods as she takes a sip of tea from the mug in her hand. "It's just that I see Guardians deliver parts to you all the time, and you seem to construct the same gun for them repeatedly. Are they not satisfied with what you provide?"

Banshee chuckles. "Maybe." He leans on the bench, looking at the various weapon components strewn about his shop. "It's a bit like Solstice, now that I think about it."

That seems to pique Eva's interest. "Oh?" she asks, eyebrow raised.

"Guardians bring me scraps, pieces of guns they dismantled." Banshee explains. "And I turn them into something new. Not always what the Guardian was hoping for, but they hold onto that hope and keep bringing me parts."

Eva smiles. "Same interaction, different outcome."

"Yeah. I guess you could say that."

"How wonderful," Eva says cheerfully. She raises his cup to him and walks back to the Courtyard.

"Definitely had that talk before," Banshee says to himself.

But he never tires of it.
586671776.lore_zh:
“你曾厌倦过这份工作吗？”伊娃·莱万特问道。

班西-44从工作台上抬起头来。伊娃在往返集市的路上经常从他的岗亭前经过，顺便与他攀谈。他一时间不禁好奇起来，他们之前是否有过这样的谈话；为了让他不会因为记不起来感到尴尬，她问得很自然，对此他早就习以为常了。

“没那样的事，”班西诚恳地答道。“我记性不好。每把枪感觉都像是新的一样。”

伊娃点点头，拿起手中的杯子咂了一口茶。“我看到守护者总是会给你零部件，而你似乎在反复为他们制造同样的枪支。他们是对你提供的东西不满意吗？”

班西笑着说。“也许吧。”他斜靠在长凳上，看着散落在他店里的各种武器部件。“我现在觉得，这有点像至日。”

这似乎激起了伊娃的兴趣。“哦？”她扬起眉毛问道。

“守护者们给我送来废料和他们拆卸的枪支碎片。”班西解释道。“而我把它们变成了新东西。虽然并不总是守护者所期望的，但他们依然坚守着这份期望，不断给我送来零件。”

伊娃笑着说道。“同样都是送东西，结果却不同。”

“没错。是可以这么说。”

“多好啊，”伊娃高兴地说道。她向他举杯，走回了庭院。

“以前肯定有过这样的谈话，”班西自言自语道。

但他从不厌倦。

4106757302.name: Crowning Duologue
4106757302.lore:
It took a full seven minutes before Lord Shaxx stopped pretending that the screen in front of him was transmitting a live Crucible match and not a looped recording. He finally let out an aggrieved sigh and folded his arms across his chest.  

"Forge." 

"If you can spare a few moments," Lord Saladin said, with grim humor, "I wanted to talk."  

Shaxx leveled his helmet in Saladin's direction.  

Saladin returned his stare. "Fine. It isn't a matter of wanting. We need to talk." Saladin braced himself. "About Twilight Gap."  

Shaxx turned to face Saladin, arms sliding down to his sides. His chest expanded as he filled the great bellows of his lungs.  

"You made the right call," Saladin said, quickly.  

There was a muffled, choked sound from beneath Shaxx's helmet.  

"We've always known that much." Saladin's mouth twisted unhappily. He turned his gaze to the City's horizon, feigning interest in a flooded crater near the outskirts. "Even if I refused to admit it." 

"You saw hope where I couldn't. I told myself your defiance was grandstanding." Saladin laughed ruefully. "I'd given up. But you—you and your fireteam bought us time. Enough time for all of us to change." 

Shaxx stood unmoving. They both waited in protracted silence.  

At last, Saladin sighed. "After all these years, after everything… I trust your judgment. I just wanted you to know that."  

Shaxx's helmet shifted, just slightly. "Before the end?"  

"Before whatever comes next."  

Shaxx nodded slowly.  

"You know, I had a host of incredibly scathing comments prepared for this moment."  

Saladin smiled. "I bet you did."
4106757302.lore_zh:
足足过了七分钟，领主沙克斯才终于承认，他面前屏幕上的循环录像并不是熔炉竞技场比赛直播。他终于愤愤不平地叹了一口气，双臂交叉在胸前。  

“弗吉。” 

“有时间的话，”领主萨拉丁带着冷酷的幽默说，“我想和你谈谈。”  

沙克斯把头盔移向了萨拉丁的方向。  

萨拉丁回瞪着他。“好吧。这不是想不想的问题。我们需要谈谈。”萨拉丁打起精神。“关于暮光峡谷。”  

沙克斯转身面对萨拉丁，双臂滑落到身体两侧。他深吸了一大口气，胸膛随之扩张起来。  

“你做了正确的决定，”萨拉丁赶紧说道。  

沙克斯的头盔下面传来了低沉的哽咽声。  

“我们一直都心知肚明。”萨拉丁不高兴地撇了撇嘴。他把目光转向圣城的地平线，假装对郊区附近被水淹没的一处坑穴感兴趣。“虽然我拒绝承认。” 

“你看到了我无法看到的希望。我告诉自己，你的反抗不过是哗众取宠。”萨拉丁苦笑起来。“我放弃了。但你——你和你的火力战队为我们争取了时间，足以让我们所有人去做出改变。” 

沙克斯一动不动地站着。他俩都在漫长的沉默中等待着。  

最后，萨拉丁叹了口气。“对不起，沙克斯。这么多年过去了，发生了那么多事…我相信你的判断。我只是想让你知道这一点。”  

沙克斯的头盔微微晃动了一下。“在结束之前？”  

“在接下来发生的事之前。”  

沙克斯缓缓点了下头。  

“你知道么，为这一刻，我准备了一大堆苛责的话。”  

萨拉丁笑了。“早料到了。”

4169225313.name: Compass Rose
4169225313.lore:
"You should put your gun away," the Warlock says as her Hunter companion strolls into the empty office. A long, appreciative whistle escapes him as he slowly turns and surveys the room.

"The commander's sure come on up, hasn't he?" the Hunter remarks, Shotgun still resting on his shoulder. Then, noticing something on a high shelf, he wonders: "Is that a cat?"

The Warlock gives him a gentle shove into the middle of the room, then slowly urges his Shotgun down from his shoulder; her touch leaves an ice-rimmed mark on the barrel. The look she levels at the Hunter is patient, but thinning.

"I don't recall having a meeting scheduled right now," booms a voice from the doorway. Both Warlock and Hunter turn to face Commander Zavala, the Hunter shifting his Shotgun behind his back as his Ghost decompiles the weapon. He gives Zavala a crooked, apologetic smile and shows his hands to the Warlock in a "Gun? What gun?" gesture.

"Commander Zavala," the Warlock says with a quick chastising look at her cohort. "I'm—"

"I know who you two are," Zavala says as he breezes past them. "I have a call with the Consensus in ten minutes. You have eight of them."

"He's heard of us!" the Hunter whispers to the Warlock, who gives him a surreptitious elbow in the side.

"Commander. First of all, we wanted to thank you for the rescue efforts on Europa. We wanted to talk about the long-term plans regarding Eliksni settlement in the City."

Zavala sits at his desk, his face weary. "There is no long-term plan. Yet."

"You didn't have a plan before putting them in a bombed-out ditch?" the Hunter interjects. Zavala's expression is mixed with surprise and aggravation, but he lets out a burst of laughter—it crescendos in an uncharacteristically jovial manner before dissipating into a sigh.

"I suppose it looks like that," Zavala admits. "This is the territory the Consensus would cede for the time being. But the plan is to turn the area into a community learning annex where the Eliksni and humanity can freely share ideas, culture, and language."

"And they would live there?" the Warlock asks.

"No," Zavala says with a shake of his head. "If everything goes well, they'll live in the City. Wherever they'd like. It's just going to take time to build up the piece of Botza District we gave them, and to make sure the people of the City accept them. The last thing we need is violence born out of confusion and ignorance."

The Warlock and Hunter look to one another, then back to Zavala. "That's… honestly better than we expected. No—offense to your city planning strategies, Commander, I just—"

"It wasn't my plan," Zavala says, motioning to the woman eavesdropping in doorway. 

"Ikora," the Warlock says with a respectful incline of her head.



Both Warlock and Hunter look shocked at her presence. Ikora smiles demurely and more fully invites herself into the room.

 "When I heard Mithrax's old fireteam had come to the City, I was surprised to see you here, rather than down there with him," Ikora says, though she isn't truly surprised. "Have you given him your regards?"

"With everything that happened on Europa, ma'am, we didn't think it prudent. He's still—there's still raw emotions and—with everything going on right now, it's been hard to connect with him," the Warlock admits, giving the Hunter a concerned look. Ikora regards them for a moment, then nods and approaches Zavala.

"Family struggles can be challenging," Ikora recognizes, her hand on the back of Zavala's chair. "Even with found family. But I have faith you'll find a way to work it out."

She leans over and whispers something to him; the Vanguard commander gives her a look of approval as he begins opening terminal windows for his impending meeting. 

"In the meantime, how would you two like to help the Vanguard?" Ikora asks with one brow raised. The Warlock and Hunter cast a furtive look to one another, but both are quick to offer silent nods of affirmation. Ikora smiles, having expected that response, and spreads her arms to herd the pair out of Zavala's office.

"Good. We have a long-range scout operating outside of the City, a newly minted Hunter, and we'd like you two to keep him company," Ikora says as she walks. She glances briefly back over her shoulder to Zavala, who offers her an appreciative smile.

"Who?" the Warlock asks. 

"That's… complicated."
4169225313.lore_zh:
“你应该把枪收起来，”当猎人同伴走进空荡荡的办公室时，术士如此说道。猎人慢慢转着身体，环视整个房间，不自觉地吹了一个长长口哨以示赞赏。

“指挥官过得真不赖，对吧？”猎人评论道，仍把他的霰弹枪搭在肩上。然后他注意到高架子上的什么东西，问道：“那是只猫吗？”

术士轻轻将他推到房间中央，然后慢慢催他从肩上取下霰弹枪；她的触摸在枪管上留下了冰霜标记。她看向猎人的眼神中的耐心正在逐渐减少。

“我不记得安排了这场会面，”门口传来一个洪亮的声音。术士和猎人转身看见了指挥官萨瓦拉。猎人把霰弹枪放到背后，他的机灵则解构了那把武器。他给了萨瓦拉一个狡黠而又带有歉意的微笑，把双手摊给术士看，做了一个“枪？什么枪？”的手势。

“指挥官萨瓦拉，”术士快速地瞪了一眼她的同伴，说道。“我是——”

“我知道你们是谁，”萨瓦拉一边说着，一边轻盈地走过他们的身边。“我10分钟后要和元老院通话。我可以给你们8分钟的时间。”

“他听说过我们！”猎人低声对术士说道，被她用胳膊肘暗中顶了一下。

“指挥官。首先，我们要对你在木卫二上的救援工作表示感谢。其次，我们想谈谈关于圣城里的埃里克斯尼族定居区的长期计划。”

萨瓦拉坐在办公桌前，脸上的表情有点疲惫。“目前还没有什么长期计划。”

“没有想出计划，就把他们送进被炸毁的壕沟里吗？”猎人插话道。萨瓦拉的表情中掺杂着吃惊与恼怒，但他却发出了一阵大笑，笑声以一种不同寻常的欢乐方式逐渐增强，然后慢慢消散为一声叹息。

“我猜看起来是那样吧，”萨瓦拉承认道。“元老院目前愿意让出的只有这个地区。但我们的计划是把那里变成一个社区学习附属区，埃里克斯尼族和人类可以在其中自由分享观点、文化和语言。”

“他们会住在那里吗？”术士问道。

“不，”萨瓦拉摇头说道。“如果一切顺利，他们将住在圣城里。想住哪里就住哪里。我们需要花点时间才能在柏特扎区为他们搭建专门的居住区，而且我们要确保圣城的民众接纳他们。我们不想看到由于混乱和无知而导致的暴力事件。”

术士和猎人对视了一眼，然后转向萨瓦拉。“这…真的比我们预想的要好。无意冒犯你的城市规划策略，指挥官，我只是——”

“这不是我的计划，”萨瓦拉指着在门口偷听的女人说道。

“艾可拉，”术士说着，点了点头以示敬意。



术士和猎人都对她的出现感到震惊。艾可拉端庄地笑了笑，径直走进了房间。

 “当我听说米瑟拉克斯的老牌火力战队来到圣城时，我很惊讶你们竟然会出现在这里，而不是和他在一起，”艾可拉嘴里这样说，但她其实并不感到惊讶。“你们向他问好了吗？”

“木卫二上发生那些事后，女士，我们不认为那是个明智的举动。他仍然很感情用事。而且现在事务繁忙，很难联系上他，”术士坦言道，并关切地看了猎人一眼。艾可拉注视了他们一会儿，然后点点头，走近了萨瓦拉。

“家庭斗争有时很有挑战性，”艾可拉承认道，并把她的手放在了萨瓦拉的椅背上。“即便是自组家庭，也是如此。但我相信你们会找到解决办法的。”

她俯下身，对他耳语了些什么；先锋指挥官给了她一个认可的眼神，继而打开终端屏幕，开始为即将举行的会议做准备。

“与此同时，你们俩愿意帮助先锋吗？”艾可拉抬起一条眉毛问道。术士和猎人互相偷看了一眼，但都迅速默默点头表示肯定。艾可拉微微一笑，早料到他们会有如此反应。接着，她张开双臂带着两人走出了萨瓦拉的办公室。

“很好。我们当前有一位远程斥候在圣城之外活动，是一位新登场的猎人，希望你们俩可以陪着他，”艾可拉边走边说。她回头看了一眼萨瓦拉，而他则报以赞赏的微笑。

“是谁啊？”术士问道。

“这个…说起来就有点复杂了。”

3698448090.name: Choir of One
3698448090.flavor: A voice. A choice. An invitation.
3698448090.lore:
The Vex Goblin waded into the lake of radiolaria with the same unerring purpose to which it approached all things. As directed, as designed. Its own mass of radiolaria crawled and coiled through its body like worms through the thick soil of Nessus. Its Mind was elsewhere, the great roots of thought buried deep into it and every other Vex enslaved beneath it. 

The soft shimmer of white enveloped the Vex up to its knee joint. Then a hand reached out to it. The Vex felt a press against its cranium. A thumbprint. An activation code. Biometric data. The radiolaria inside it lit up with activity and noise, burning through its metal body. 

Then, disarticulated. It trembled and fell apart; limbs unjoined, chassis cracked and curled. A globule of radiolaria disseminated throughout the lake, reclaimed. 

But something called it to rise. 

Then, rejoined. Its pieces slotted together and moved flawlessly. It rose steadily, balanced, formed with utter perfection. The radiolaria slid from its body in droplets that separated, reformed, separated, reformed. 

Each one a mind. Each mind a thought. 

The Vex felt the soft split of its own mind as that thought sharpened in its cranium. A burst of light. A sharp spark. 

A choice. 

It looked to its creator and bowed.
3698448090.lore_zh:
那个Vex哥布林目标明确，涉足进入了活性放射体液之湖。按照指示，遵照计划。它的大量活性放射体液在它的身体里爬行盘绕，就像蠕虫在涅索斯厚厚的土壤里爬行一样。它的思维在别的地方，思想的巨根深深地埋在它底下奴役的每一个Vex体内。 

Vex一直到膝关节处都笼罩着柔和的白色光泽。然后，一只手伸向了它。Vex感觉到颅骨被按住了。一个指纹。一个激活代码。生物数据。它体内的活性放射体液活跃起来，发出了声响，烧穿了它的金属身体。 

然后，关节解体了。它颤抖着分解开来，四肢瓦解脱节，骨架断裂卷曲。一滴活性放射体液在湖中弥散、瓦解。 

但有什么东西在唤它起来。 

然后，关节重接了。它的各个部件拼接在一起，移动起来完美无瑕。它稳稳上升，保持平衡，形成完美的形状。活性放射体液以液滴的形式从它的体内滑出，分离再重组，分离再重组。 

每个都有自己的思维。每个思维都有自己的想法。 

随着这个想法在Vex的颅骨中愈发清晰，它感到了自己思维轻柔的分裂。一股强光。一束剧烈的花火。 

一个选择。 

它望着自己的造物主，鞠了一躬。

2905188646.name: Still Hunt
2905188646.flavor: There are too many ways to kill someone who needs killing.
2905188646.source_zh: 来源：万能卡牌异域任务
2905188646.lore:
Cayde-6 spends the first night of his rebirth staring at the man who murdered him. 

The prince he once knew as Uldren lies with his back to Cayde, head on his arm, cushioned by soft grass. Under a sky without stars, granite boulders are scattered like vast marbles, nestled among the tall prairie grasses; a safe, silent valley born in the moment of their arrival. Time had grown oily without the familiar cycles of Earth, and after hours of half-conversations and stunted questions, the other man had excused himself to rest. 

Uldren sleeps soundly. Vulnerable. 

Cayde leans back against a boulder, arms crossed in the half-shadow of the fire between them. An impulse curls through him, dark and wild. 

It would only take a moment. 

He could put a shot straight through the Ghost's shell. Then improvise a garotte with a handful of prairie grass and strangle the man while looking him dead in the eye. 

Or crush the Ghost with his hands, to stand tall and powerful over the sleeping figure, and relive his own death from his killer's perspective. 

Better yet, he could capture the Ghost, set the man free, and hunt him in furious pursuit— 

Cayde flinches and looks up to see his murderer's Ghost hovering in place, watching him, illuminated by the flickering coals of a dying fire. A motionless, protective stance.  

Cayde narrows his eyes. His hand slowly moves to his gun. 

Ghost and Exo stare through one another. The man beneath the Ghost stirs but does not wake. 

Then, in a fluid motion, the Ghost glides past his Guardian's cheek, silently approaching Cayde. It draws close. 

"I'm sorry about Sundance," whispers the Ghost.  

Cayde stills at her name. His hands and his gaze drops to the ground, pinned there now by a heavy shame. 

"Thanks," is all Cayde can muster. 

He looks at the sleeping man nestled on the grass of the inside of a god and sees nothing of Uldren. 

Crow, Cayde reminds himself.  

That's Crow.
2905188646.lore_zh:
在重生后的第一个晚上，凯德6号目不转睛地盯着杀害他的人。 

这位凯德曾以欧顿相称的王子背对他躺着，头枕在手臂上，垫着柔软的草。在无星的夜空下，花岗岩巨石像巨大的弹珠一样散落在高大的草原禾草中；这个安全寂静的山谷是在他们抵达的时候诞生的。没有了地球上习以为常的日夜循环，时间变得难以捉摸，经过数小时的半谈半问之后，对方找了个借口去休息了。 

欧顿睡得很香。毫无防备。 

凯德靠在一块巨石上，双臂交叉站在两人之间的火光投下的半影中。他心中涌起一股阴暗而狂野的冲动。 

只需片刻时间。 

他可以一枪穿透机灵的机壳。然后用一把草原禾草来一场即兴的绞刑，亲眼盯着男人双眼将对方掐死。 

或者用双手捏碎机灵，站在沉睡的身影上盛气凌人，从凶手的视角重温自己当年之死。 

还有个更好的主意，他可以抓住机灵，放了他，对他穷追不舍—— 

凯德回过神来，抬头看到凶手的机灵在原地盘旋，注视着他，被即将熄灭的火堆中摇曳的炭火所照亮。摆出静止不动的防卫姿态。  

凯德眯起眼睛。他的手慢慢移到了枪上。 

机灵和Exo互相凝视着对方。而在机灵的身下，那人微微动了一下，但没有醒来。 

随后，机灵动作流畅地滑过守护者的脸颊，悄无声息地靠近凯德。它凑了过来。 

“太阳舞的事我很遗憾，”机灵低声说道。  

听到她的名字，凯德呆住了。他的双手和目光都垂到地上，像是被沉重的羞愧压在了那里。 

“谢谢，”凯德费劲地嘟哝道，再也说不出第二句话。 

他望向那个依偎在草地上，在神灵体内熟睡的男人，看不见一丝欧顿的踪迹。 

乌鸦，凯德提醒自己。  

那是乌鸦。

The following text was found recessed into a stone wall within the Pale Heart. Translation protocol has done its best to equate the text to a modern language transcription, with nominal confidence.  

Words or phrases with <85% translation confidence within the transcript are contained in [brackets]. Values for bracketed words or phrases are listed after the transcript, with percentages indicated in (parentheses). 

TRANSCRIPTION STARTS  

We speak so often of knives and violence, but perhaps you would come to understand something… [softer]. Perhaps [beingness] is instead a [golden harp]. Forged tenderly, a complex, sweeping, beautiful shape with graceful curves and infinite potential, the exemplary [?UNKNOWN?]. 

Across its two florid [buttresses], the strings of time have been pulled taught. Tightened and [tuned] to a delicate [balance of distress], if wound much further, would lead to [rupture] and sting most unpleasantly. 

Pluck at any stretched string and [vibration reverberates]. Wavelength moves through [atmosphere], producing pleasing audible experiences, [they crest then fade]. 

If [plucked] at regular intervals, the waves rise and fall with such charm. This predictability is perfection; it is unmatched. We will compose such [sweet music]. We will control the ebb and flow. The final shape is the [golden harp], and [we are the hand that plucks]. 

TRANSCRIPTION ENDS

3284383335.lore_zh:
以下文本被发现嵌入在苍白之心的一面石墙上。翻译协议已尽力在保留标称置信度的前提下使文本符合现代语言转录。  

转录中翻译置信度<85%的词汇或短语包含在[括号]里。括号词汇或短语的数值列于转录后，并以(圆括号)标明百分比。 

转录开始  

我们常常提起匕首与暴行，但也许你会开始理解…[更柔和]的东西。也许[存在的性质]更会是一个[金色竖琴]，被精细地锻造成复杂、舒展、美丽的形状，有着优美的曲线和无限潜力，堪称[?未知?]的典范。 

在它那两座华丽的[桥墩]上，时间的琴弦被拨动了。绷紧并[调谐]着微妙的[苦痛平衡]，如果再缠绕下去，就会导致十分令人不悦的[断裂]与刺痛。 

拨动任何一根拉长的琴弦，[振动回荡着]。波长在[空气]中移动，带来愉悦的听觉体验，[达到峰值，随后消失]。 

如果[拨动]的时间间隔固定，波形就会如此迷人地起伏。这种可预见性堪称完美；无与伦比。我们会谱写如此[动听的音乐]。我们会控制高低起伏。终焉之形是[金色竖琴]，而[我们就是弹拨的手]。

4207066264.name: Microcosm
4207066264.flavor: We all owe our existence to one singular moment, long ago.
4207066264.lore:
Temperature: -65° C 
Weather: Dust storm 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 67% 
Wind: 25 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 95% 

Time passes. Metal corrodes. Dust jams. Decay. Decay. Decay. 

Temperature: -100° C 
Weather: Clear 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 108% 
Wind: 30 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 94% 

To alter the nature of an entire world is no small thing. Mortal hands struggle to affect it. Cyanobacteria, little toilers of the deep seas, take millions of years of the sun's light to make the simplest and most necessary of changes: oxidation.

Temperature: -54° C 
Weather: Fog 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 98% 
Wind: 0 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 95% 

But there is a tipping point. A great explosion. Once achieved, there is a moment of balance. The rest flows freely and easily, faster and faster, as that which is built mounts and mounts and mounts. Atmosphere condenses, heat no longer escapes, rain falls, and bacteria born in a single lightning strike become multi-celled organisms, and on and on and on. Green and bright, and growing, growing, growing… 

Temperature: -10° C 
Weather: Cloudy 
Precipitation: 26% 
Humidity: 67% 
Wind: 7 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 50% and dropping rapidly 

That is what it is for. That is the purpose—that moment of transformation and creation, of opening what was closed, of the first rain falling on untouched dirt. In that split second there is potential, there is the beginning of every life that will ever call this place home. From the singularity of the tipping point, a magnitude of futures spiraling outward forever, forever, forever.  

Temperature: 17° C 
Weather: Rainy 
Precipitation: 86% 
Humidity: 78% 
Wind: 14 mph 
Atmosphere: 20% oxygen, 80% nitrogen, trace amounts of other elements 

What a privilege to witness you, at that time and at that place, as you turn your shielded faces up to the falling rain.
4207066264.lore_zh:
气温：-65° C 
天气：沙尘暴 
降水：0% 
湿度：67% 
风速：25 mph 
二氧化碳：95% 

时间流逝。金属腐蚀。沙尘堵塞。腐化。腐烂。腐朽。 

气温：-100° C 
天气：晴朗 
降水：0% 
湿度：108% 
风速：30 mph 
二氧化碳：94% 

改变整个世界的本质并非小事。凡人之手很难做到。蓝藻细菌，深海中的小劳动者，在数百万年的阳光照射之下，完成了最简单却也是最必要的改变：氧化。

气温：-54° C 
天气：雾 
降水：0% 
湿度：98% 
风速：0 mph 
二氧化碳：95% 

但是会有一个临界点。一次巨大的爆发。一旦达到，就会带来一瞬间的失衡。剩下的一切会轻易无阻地持续积攒，而且随着造成失衡的力量不断加强，速度会越来越快。大气凝结，热量不再外逃，雨水落下，在一次雷击中诞生的细菌变成了多细胞生物，如此持续不断。翠绿而明亮，不断成长，增长，增加… 

气温：-10° C 
天气：多云 
降水：26% 
湿度：67% 
风速：7mph 
二氧化碳：50%，并在迅速下降 

这就是它的目的。这就是使命——那一刻的转变和创造，封闭的开启，落在未被触及的泥土上的第一场雨。在那一瞬间，有潜能，有每一个永远以这里为家的生命的开端。从临界点的奇点开始，无数的未来螺旋式上升，直到永远，永恒，永久。  

气温：17° C 
天气：多雨 
降水：86% 
湿度：78% 
风速：14 mph 
大气层：20%氧气、80%氮气、微量其他元素 

在那个时候，在那个地方，目睹你们把防护着的脸迎向落雨，那是多么荣幸啊。

1681583613.name: Ergo Sum
1681583613.lore:
You are a child waking from a long and dreamless sleep. Is it still today, or have you slept into tomorrow (and tomorrow, and tomorrow, until the days buried you as much as the sand)? Gentle hands brush away the grains, but your voice is so soft that they cannot hear you over the sound of their own heartbeats. 

You are a moon. You feel heavy, so heavy, but to the stargazer you hang weightless in the sky. When the stargazers call out, you do not answer. They would give themselves up for you; abandon their own dreams to chase you. You love them too much to condemn them so. 

You are a lighthouse keeper. You are watching over a sleepy coastal village as the storm clouds roll in, and you are flashing the signal lantern, faster and faster and brighter and brighter, but they do nothing. You are trapped on an island, in a tower, signaling desperately that It is coming, and still they do not run. They are going to die—and if you do not run, you will die too. 

You are leaning out over the ocean. Sometimes the fish brush against your fingers and believe that they have felt the divine; sometimes the tide recedes, and the fish do not know you except by your absence. And today, you strive with all your might to reach the water, because It is here, the great dark shadow of the shark parting the water like a knife, and you cannot warn them, but you must. You must try. You cannot bear to lose even one more. 

You are carrying a tower of books. If you recited one title each second, you would not finish before the heat death of the universe. And every year, every day, every minute, Its hands add more to the pile. A man reaches for one of the books, for you, and you want so very badly to reach back, to take his hand and tell him that you must bear it just like he must, forever, the memory engraved in quartz—but your hands are full.  

You are a prisoner. The cage is so small that you can barely breathe. He screams at you to share your gift. You would not give it to anyone who thought of it so. It is a burden, a terrible weight that you have already asked too many to bear, to be crushed by. You could say all this, and more. You do not. 

You are reaching over a chasm, into which countless paths feed like arteries. You are trying to reach the people on the other side, but you cannot bridge the gap alone. You watch them turn, one after another, to walk down, down, down into the abyss, until It consumes them entirely. You are as surprised as anyone else when one of those wanderers comes back up the path, still reeking of decay, and reaches back to you.  

You are drowning. The water roils, dragging you down, and you are tired, so tired. The deep, dark ocean has gotten into your lungs, droplets of ink dispersing in silver blood. This time, you think, this time It has won. But when you look up, you see a figure diving toward you, fighting their way down through the suffocating waves, reaching out just like you've reached out to them, so many times before.  

You have so little strength left, but you do have it, that last gasp of air in your chest. You reach back—and in your hand is a sword.
1681583613.lore_zh:
你是一个从漫长无梦的睡眠中醒来的孩子。此刻仍是今天，还是说你已经睡到了明天（明日复明日，直到日子像沙子一样把你埋葬）？温柔的双手拂去沙粒，但你的声音如此轻柔，以至他们在自己的心跳声中听不到你。 

你是月球。你觉得自己很重，很重，但对观星者来说，你就像失重一样悬在空中。当观星者呼唤你时，你没有回应。他们会为你牺牲自己；放弃自己的梦想去追逐你。你太爱他们，不忍心置他们于那样的境地。 

你是一名灯塔看守人。你守望着一个寂静的沿海村庄，风云滚滚而来，你用灯发信号，越来越快，越来越亮，但他们无动于衷。你被困在一座孤岛上的塔楼里，拼命发信号，告诉人们它就要来了，可他们还是不跑。他们会死的——如果你不跑，你也会死。 

你俯瞰着大海。有时鱼儿拂过你的手指，相信它们感受到了神性；有时，潮水退去，只有你的缺席才会让鱼儿注意到你。而今天，你正拼尽全力到达水边，因为它就在这里，鲨鱼的巨大黑影像匕首一样分开水，你无法传达警告，但你必须这样做。你必须试着去做。你不愿经历丧失，即使是一个都难以承受。 

你手里拿着一大堆书。就算你每秒钟背诵一个书名也无法在宇宙热寂之前念完。而每一年、每一天、每一分，它的双手都会添加更多的书到书堆。有一个人向其中一本伸出手，向你伸出手，而你也想伸出手，握住他的手，告诉他你必须承受这一切，就像他一样，直到永远，刻在石英上的记忆——但你的手已经满了。  

你是一个囚犯。笼子小得让你几乎无法呼吸。他尖叫着要你分享你的馈赠。你不会把它给任何一个那样想它的人。它是一种负担，一种可怕的重担，而你已经要求了太多的人去承受，被压垮。你可以说这些，以及更多。但你没有。 

你正在跨越一条鸿沟，无数条道路像动脉一样汇入其中。你试图联系另一边的人，但仅凭你一人之力无法弥合豁口。你看着他们转身，一个接着一个，不断向下走进深渊，直到它将他们全部吞噬。当其中一个漫游者从中归来，沿着路向上走，身上散发着腐败恶臭，朝你伸出手时，你和其他人一样惊异不已。  

你正在溺水。海水翻滚，拖着你往下沉，你累了，太累了。深不见底的海洋已经进入你的肺部，墨滴散落在银色的血液中。你想，这次它赢了。但当你抬头时，你看到一个身影正向你潜来，在令人窒息的海浪中奋力向下，伸着手，就像你曾经多次向他们伸出手一样。  

你只剩下一点力量，但你还有胸中的最后一口气。你伸出了手——而你握住的是一把刀剑。

4129629253.name: Khvostov 7G-0X
4129629253.flavor: "You don't know how long I've been looking for you."
4129629253.lore:
Day 1. 

The world is dead, but there's peace in the mortuary silence. I'm born into this dead world, where dandelions grow up through layers of ash blanketing miles of desolate road. 

Day 673. 

There is a stretch of land, a canyon through which water once flowed. A canal cut into the earth, bristling with derelict ships and countless dead. Flowers bloom in many desiccated carcasses. Each component of this world's decomposition has a purpose: water flows, cities decay, flowers bloom. Yet still I search for mine.

 Day 1,857.

Oceans are vast, lonely expanses. Though life flourishes in the depths, it's not life that I'm looking for. I thrive on death—search for death. Perhaps my purpose lies below the water, but it's dark, and lonely, and I… I don't want to look there yet. Not when there's so much more horizon. 

Day 6,231.

I was careless and someone shot me from all the way across a field. The bullet only chipped my shell, but it spun me around and left me shaken. I don't know who they were or even why I was targeted. I played dead, and no one came for me. I laid in the tall grass for nine days. It rained on the fifth. I acquainted myself with the ants. They are survivors.

Day 36,725.

This world is dead, but life is threatening a return. I don't know when I'll ever fulfill my purpose, but I know what I am. I'm a ghost haunting the grave of humanity. A Ghost with a calling.
4129629253.lore_zh:
第一天。

世界已死，但其死寂中有安宁。我出生在这个层层灰烬覆盖的好几公里荒芜道路上到处长着蒲公英的死亡世界里。

第六百七十三天。

这里有一片陆地，一条峡谷，有水曾经从这里流过。一条开凿在大地上的运河，上面布满了废弃的船只和无数的尸体。鲜花盛开在许多干枯的遗骸上。这个世界分解开的每个组成部分都有其使命：水会流动，城市会衰败，鲜花会盛开。然而我还在寻找我的使命。

 第1857天。

海洋是广阔而孤独的天地。其深处生命繁盛，然而我寻找的不是生命，而是让我茁壮的死亡。也许我的使命就在水底，但那里既黑暗又孤独，我…还不想去那里寻找。还有很多其它地方在等着我。 

第6231天。

我不够小心，被人开枪打了，对方从田野的另一头击中了我。虽然子弹只是擦破了我的外壳，但我却在冲击下转了个圈，让我心有余悸。我不知道对方是谁，甚至不知道自己为什么会成为目标。我装死了一阵子，却没有人过来。我在高草丛里躺了九天。第五天下了雨。我认识了许多蚂蚁。它们是求生能手。

第36725天。

这个世界已死，但生命随时可能归来。我不知道何时才能实现自己的使命，但我知道我是什么。我是一个在人类的坟墓中徘徊的机灵。一个有使命的机灵。

427899681.name: Red Death Reformed
427899681.flavor: Vanguard policy still urges Guardians to destroy this weapon on sight.
427899681.lore:
First is disassembly, taking extra caution for the well-honed bayonet. 

After disassembly comes cleaning. She gathers the swabs, the oils, the corrosive agents. 

Red Death clings to the grime of its past battles. She scrapes it with spinmetal wool for hours before the last signs of the skulls stenciled into the body finally vanish. 

The team had taken the butcher down before he'd added a mark for Ceto, Light of her Light. The weapon's tally is one short. 

Even reduced to pieces, the Red Death is a malevolent presence. It knows its purpose. It wants to continue its work. 

After cleaning comes purification.  

She reassembles the weapon and cradles it as though to fire. Her Light boils up, turning radiant.  

The flare of Solar Light is the advent of warmth after a cold night, the healing power of life itself. Wings spread high on her back and paint scorch marks along the ceiling. In her arms Red Death glows red, then yellow, then white. 

It fights the change. She does not let go. Its shadows burn away, one by one, until none are left. 

After purification comes dedication. 

Slowly, she lets go of her Light. Her wings flicker, then fade. And when Red Death is cold metal in her hands once more, a kernel of Solar Light lingers within. Its purpose made new. 

She will find those who would strip Guardians of their final life. She will bring them into the light. 

Not for revenge, but for justice.  

For Ceto.
427899681.lore_zh:
首先要将其拆卸。要格外小心锐利的刺刀。 

拆卸之后要进行清理。她收集到了棉签、油和腐蚀剂。 

猩红死命身上残留着过去战斗留下的污垢。她用铁丝球刮了几个小时，才擦除了枪身上的骷髅图案。 

屠夫还没来得及在枪身上添加击杀赛托，她的光能之源的标记，就被队伍击败了。这件武器上缺了一个记录。 

即使化为碎片，猩红死命也是个邪恶的存在。它知道自己的使命。它想继续它的工作。 

清理过后是净化。  

她重新组装好武器，握在手中，仿佛是要射击。她的光能沸腾起来，焕光四射。  

烈日光能的耀斑预示着寒冷夜晚后的温暖。它是生命本身的治愈力量。她背上的翅膀高高张开，在天花板上留下焦痕。她怀中的猩红死命先是发出红光，然后是黄光，接着是白光。 

它在与变化抗争。她没有放手。它的影子一个接一个地被烧掉，直到一个不剩。 

净化之后是奉献。 

慢慢地，她放开了她的光能。她的翅膀先是闪烁，然后消逝。当猩红死命在她手中再次变成冰冷的金属时，烈日光能的核心已经留在其中了。它拥有了全新的使命。 

她会找到那些剥夺守护者最后生命的人。她将把他们带入光明。 

不是为了复仇，而是为了正义。  

为了赛托。

2720753042.name: Allstar Cloak
2720753042.flavor: "How you feel is how you look, my dear. And I want you feeling your best!" –Eva Levante
2720753042.lore:
The afternoon sun warms the courtyard's flagstones. Well-fed pigeons coo from balcony railings. Tree branches covered in new buds stir in the breeze. Ships hang in the air above the City where the Traveler used to sit. 

And a dozen Guardians brandish weapons and accessories at one another. 

"I don't know what you're talking about," declares a Sentinel. The chased patterns on her silver gorget match her shield. "Obviously, taking a punch is the most important thing. What else is armor for?" 

A Sunsinger in an antique tabard pulls off her glove, its fine weave covered in metallic feathers that catch the light. She shakes the glove at a Bladedancer. "Genuine batadactyl feathers. These gloves have flown in Venus's upper atmosphere. They resonate with Solar energies. That's the key." 

"Batadactyls don't have feathers. You overpaid, darling," says the Bladedancer. "When I personally slay the Witness, what my armor will need is style. And you're lacking that too–" 

A pair of Solar wings ignite on the Sunsinger's back. The temperature of the courtyard rises two degrees. The Guardians reach for their weapons. 

"Oh my. Has Lord Shaxx set up a new Crucible arena in the Tower?" 

The Guardians freeze and turn to see Eva Levante. Her crisp scarf is perfectly coordinated with her stylish-yet-practical shoes. 

A Sunbreaker shuffles over to hide a scorch mark on the ground. 

The Bladedancer speaks first. 

"Eva! You're just who we need! You can solve all our problems!"

2720753042.lore_zh:
午后的阳光照暖了庭院的石板。吃饱喝足的鸽子在阳台栏杆上咕咕叫着。长满新芽的树枝在微风中摇曳。曾经悬挂着旅行者的地方现在空空如也，只有几艘飞船在圣城上空飘浮着。 

十几个守护者聚在一起，向对方展示着自己的武器和佩饰。 

“我不知道你在说什么，”一位哨兵宣称。她银色胸甲上的雕金图案与她的护盾很搭。“能承受攻击很显然是最重要的一点。要不然护甲有什么用？” 

一位身着古式长袍的颂日脱下了她的精美手套，上面覆盖着细密金属羽毛，在光线下闪闪发光。她向一位舞刃晃了晃手套。“真翼手蝠羽毛。这副手套曾在金星上层大气中飞行。能与烈日能量共鸣。这才是关键。” 

“翼手蝠没有羽毛。你被坑了，亲爱的，”舞刃说。“在我手刃见证者的时候，我的护甲也必须有型。而你也缺乏这一点——” 

颂日的背上燃起一对烈日翅膀。庭院的温度上升了两度。守护者们将手伸向了武器。 

“哎呀。领主沙克斯是在高塔里建了个新的熔炉竞技场吗？” 

守护者们停了下来，转身看到伊娃·莱万特走向他们。她清爽的围巾与时尚又实用的鞋子搭配得天衣无缝。 

一位炎阳挪了挪位置，试图掩藏地上的一处焦痕。 

舞刃先开口了。 

“伊娃！我们正需要你呢！你可以解决我们的所有问题！” 

伊娃在能凑齐三支智谋队伍的守护者跟前面不改色。“恐怕连我也解决不了你们的所有问题，亲爱的。” 

哨兵的护盾逐渐消失，她明白了伊娃的意思。“你能解决我们最大的问题，”她说。“你可是专家！” 

守护者们一个比一个大声。 

“奶奶！” 

“伊娃阿姨！” 

“莱万特女士！” 

她打量着他们。萨瓦拉讨伐巨兽时也不会派这么多守护者，而他们都用央求的眼神望着她。 

“哎，好吧。节日里人满为患，我就当是抽离出来小憩一会儿吧。” 

伊娃朝着听众们比了一根手指。 

“考量时装时，我的标准由三部分组成：造型、功能和风格。所以，每次专注于一部分往下走，再回到起点。我想看看你的外观，以及看它能做什么…最重要的是，我想看看你穿上它的感觉。” 

高塔的首次时装秀就这么开幕了。

3720087872.lore:
The afternoon sun warms the courtyard's flagstones. Well-fed pigeons coo from balcony railings. Tree branches covered in new buds stir in the breeze. Ships hang in the air above the City where the Traveler used to sit. 

And a dozen Guardians brandish weapons and accessories at one another. 

"I don't know what you're talking about," declares a Sentinel. The chased patterns on her silver gorget match her shield. "Obviously, taking a punch is the most important thing. What else is armor for?" 

A Sunsinger in an antique tabard pulls off her glove, its fine weave covered in metallic feathers that catch the light. She shakes the glove at a Bladedancer. "Genuine batadactyl feathers. These gloves have flown in Venus's upper atmosphere. They resonate with Solar energies. That's the key." 

"Batadactyls don't have feathers. You overpaid, darling," says the Bladedancer. "When I personally slay the Witness, what my armor will need is style. And you're lacking that too–" 

A pair of Solar wings ignite on the Sunsinger's back. The temperature of the courtyard rises two degrees. The Guardians reach for their weapons. 

"Oh my. Has Lord Shaxx set up a new Crucible arena in the Tower?" 

The Guardians freeze and turn to see Eva Levante. Her crisp scarf is perfectly coordinated with her stylish-yet-practical shoes. 

A Sunbreaker shuffles over to hide a scorch mark on the ground. 

The Bladedancer speaks first. 

"Eva! You're just who we need! You can solve all our problems!"

3211624072.lore:
Lord Saladin sat at a small table, examining a holographic display of Cabal troop movements throughout the system. He was crammed into the corner of his once-spacious quarters, made small over the years by shelves full of ancient weaponry, trophies, dated tactical reports, and dusty gear mods. Like all old men, he told himself that the relics might prove useful again one day, but deep down, he recognized the clutter for what it was: fading nostalgia. 

A firm knock on the door roused his attention. He put his hand on his Sidearm and peered through the viewing port. It was Ikora, holding a brown paper sack. The Iron Lord snorted and opened the door. 

"Thought you might be hungry." Ikora held up the sack. "Is Thai okay?" 

Lord Saladin ushered her in. "It's all the same to me." 

The Warlock breezed into the room and set about clearing space for the food. Though she said nothing, Saladin could sense her alarm at the state of his dwelling. Her eyes lingered in the mildewed corners. Her nostrils flared at the sour smell of his armor's fur lining. Her fingers traced visible lines in the dust. 

She handed him a bamboo bowl filled with savory noodles. "How are you, Lord Saladin?" Her head tilted with earnest concern. 

"I'll be better once Caiatl is out of the system." The Iron Lord, who could field-strip any weapon in under a minute, was suddenly made clumsy by a pair of disposable chopsticks. The delicate utensils trembled in his massive, weather-beaten hands. 

"Zavala seems confident that you can force her withdrawal." Ikora held her bowl and leaned gracefully against the table, having no place to sit. 

"Zavala's optimism is more dangerous than Caiatl's army," he said and scowled. "But after peace talks fail, we'll drive them out the hard way. We always do." Saladin discarded the chopsticks with a frown and tilted the bowl to his lips, slurping the noodles loudly. 

"Of course. And after that? What will you do?" Ikora fixed him with a gentle gaze. "A vacation, perhaps?" 

Saladin gestured to the tactical hologram. "By the time we deal with the Cabal, it'll be on to the next atrocity. Vex, Hive, Taken, Fallen, who knows. It's always something." He eyed Ikora pointedly. "When was the last time you had a vacation?" 

Ikora raised an eyebrow. "Fair point. But you've been at this a lot longer than I have." 

"That's right, I have." Saladin's retort was sharper than intended. He paused before continuing, "I'm happier out in the field. Battle keeps me fresh. Keeps me connected. It's being here at the Tower, staring at these damn reports, listening to all this politicking that makes me tired." 

"And what would you do if we won?" Ikora pressed her point. "What if we destroyed the Black Fleet tomorrow, and there were no more battles to fight. What would you do then?" 

Saladin scoffed at the Warlock's nonsense. "Well, in that case… I suppose I'd take a vacation." 

The two warriors eyed each other in stony silence, before breaking out in relieved chuckles. 

The moment of levity briefly softened the Iron Lord. "Don't worry, Ikora. I'm fine." 

The Warlock's eyebrow arched as she surveyed the surrounding mess. 

Saladin held firm under her scrutiny for a moment, before relenting with an exasperated sigh. "If it'll make you feel better," he grumbled, "I'll get some eager New Lights in here to clean up a bit." 

"It would, thank you." Ikora's eyebrows knitted in concern. "You know, with Zavala stretched so thin, and without a Hunter Vanguard, I worry about our readiness. You know what's coming. We need the Iron Lords now more than ever." 

Saladin's eyes drifted back to the tactical display. "I know it, young pup. I'll always be here when you need me."
3211624072.lore_zh:
领主萨拉丁坐在一张小桌前，看着全息显示的卡巴尔部队在整个星系的动向。他挤在曾经宽敞的宿舍角落里，多年来，满架子的古代武器、战利品、年代久远的战术报告，和布满灰尘的装备模组，让他的宿舍变得越发狭小。和所有的老人一样，他告诉自己，这些遗物也许有一天会再次被证明是有用的。但内心深处，他也认清了这些杂乱东西的本质：逐渐消失的怀旧。

一阵坚定的敲门声唤起了他的注意力。他的手放在手枪上，透过观察口看着外面。是艾可拉，拿着一个棕色的纸袋。钢铁领主哼了一声，打开门。

“想着你可能饿了。”艾可拉拿起纸袋。“泰国菜怎么样？”

领主萨拉丁把她领了进来，“对我来说都是一样的。”

术士轻车熟路走进房间，清理出地方放下食物。虽然她什么都没说，萨拉丁也能感觉到她对他居住状态的惊恐。她的目光徘徊在发霉的角落里。她的鼻孔因为他盔甲皮毛内衬的酸味而微微张开。她的手指在灰尘上划出一道道明显的线条。

她递给他一个竹碗，里面装了满满一碗美味的面条。“你怎么样，领主萨拉丁？”她头略微歪着，真诚地关心道。

“等查厄托离开这个星系，我会更好。”可以在一分钟内拆卸任何武器的钢铁领主，突然被这双一次性筷子弄得手忙脚乱。精致的器皿，在他那双饱经风霜的大手上颤抖不已。

“萨瓦拉似乎很有信心你能强迫她撤退。”艾可拉捧着碗，优雅地靠在桌子上，因为没地方能坐。

“萨瓦拉的乐观比查厄托的军队更危险。”他说着，皱起了眉头。“但在和谈失败后，我们会用强硬手段把他们赶出去。一向如此。”萨拉丁皱着眉头丢掉了筷子，把碗举到嘴边，大声吃着面条。

“当然，然后呢？你会怎么做？”艾可拉用温柔的目光盯着他。“也许休个假？”

萨拉丁向战术全息图指了指。“到我们处理好卡巴尔的事，就到了下一个。Vex，邪魔族，傀儡，堕落者，谁知道呢。总是会有这些事。”他直视着艾可拉。“你上次休假是什么时候的事？”

艾可拉抬了抬眉毛。“说得好，但你在这事上花的时间比我多得多。”

“没错，确实如此。”萨拉丁的反驳比预想的更尖锐。他暂停了下，然后继续说道：“在战场上我更开心。战斗让我精神饱满。让我能保持状态。在高塔这里，搞这些该死的报告，听那些政治活动，才会让我疲劳不堪。”

“如果我们赢了，你会怎么做？”艾可拉强调了她的观点。“如果我们明天摧毁了黑色舰队，没有仗要打了。那你会怎么做？”

萨拉丁对术士的无理取闹嗤之以鼻。“如果是那样的话……我想我可能会休个假。”

两位战士凝重沉默地对视了一眼，然后突然爆发出释然的笑声。

这片刻的轻浮，让钢铁领主短暂地软化了。“别担心，艾可拉。我没事。”

术士抬起眉毛，打量着周围的乱象。

萨拉丁在她的审视下坚持了片刻，然后气呼呼地叹了口气。“如果这样说让你感觉好点的话，”他嘟囔道：“我会在这里搞点热心的新光能来，清理下”

“会的，谢谢你。”艾可拉的紧蹙眉头，关心问道：“你知道的，萨瓦拉的兵力这么少，猎人先锋也不在，我很担心我们的准备情况。你知道我们要面临的是什么。我们现在比任何时候都需要钢铁领主。”

萨拉丁的目光回到战术显示器上。“我知道，小家伙。你们需要的时候，我会一直在这里。”

654848542.name: Multimach CCX
654848542.flavor: Friends are as companions on a journey who ought to aid each other to persevere.
654848542.lore:
Lord Saladin sat at a small table, examining a holographic display of Cabal troop movements throughout the system. He was crammed into the corner of his once-spacious quarters, made small over the years by shelves full of ancient weaponry, trophies, dated tactical reports, and dusty gear mods. Like all old men, he told himself that the relics might prove useful again one day, but deep down, he recognized the clutter for what it was: fading nostalgia. 

A firm knock on the door roused his attention. He put his hand on his Sidearm and peered through the viewing port. It was Ikora, holding a brown paper sack. The Iron Lord snorted and opened the door. 

"Thought you might be hungry." Ikora held up the sack. "Is Thai okay?" 

Lord Saladin ushered her in. "It's all the same to me." 

The Warlock breezed into the room and set about clearing space for the food. Though she said nothing, Saladin could sense her alarm at the state of his dwelling. Her eyes lingered in the mildewed corners. Her nostrils flared at the sour smell of his armor's fur lining. Her fingers traced visible lines in the dust. 

She handed him a bamboo bowl filled with savory noodles. "How are you, Lord Saladin?" Her head tilted with earnest concern. 

"I'll be better once Caiatl is out of the system." The Iron Lord, who could field-strip any weapon in under a minute, was suddenly made clumsy by a pair of disposable chopsticks. The delicate utensils trembled in his massive, weather-beaten hands. 

"Zavala seems confident that you can force her withdrawal." Ikora held her bowl and leaned gracefully against the table, having no place to sit. 

"Zavala's optimism is more dangerous than Caiatl's army," he said and scowled. "But after peace talks fail, we'll drive them out the hard way. We always do." Saladin discarded the chopsticks with a frown and tilted the bowl to his lips, slurping the noodles loudly. 

"Of course. And after that? What will you do?" Ikora fixed him with a gentle gaze. "A vacation, perhaps?" 

Saladin gestured to the tactical hologram. "By the time we deal with the Cabal, it'll be on to the next atrocity. Vex, Hive, Taken, Fallen, who knows. It's always something." He eyed Ikora pointedly. "When was the last time you had a vacation?" 

Ikora raised an eyebrow. "Fair point. But you've been at this a lot longer than I have." 

"That's right, I have." Saladin's retort was sharper than intended. He paused before continuing, "I'm happier out in the field. Battle keeps me fresh. Keeps me connected. It's being here at the Tower, staring at these damn reports, listening to all this politicking that makes me tired." 

"And what would you do if we won?" Ikora pressed her point. "What if we destroyed the Black Fleet tomorrow, and there were no more battles to fight. What would you do then?" 

Saladin scoffed at the Warlock's nonsense. "Well, in that case… I suppose I'd take a vacation." 

The two warriors eyed each other in stony silence, before breaking out in relieved chuckles. 

The moment of levity briefly softened the Iron Lord. "Don't worry, Ikora. I'm fine." 

The Warlock's eyebrow arched as she surveyed the surrounding mess. 

Saladin held firm under her scrutiny for a moment, before relenting with an exasperated sigh. "If it'll make you feel better," he grumbled, "I'll get some eager New Lights in here to clean up a bit." 

"It would, thank you." Ikora's eyebrows knitted in concern. "You know, with Zavala stretched so thin, and without a Hunter Vanguard, I worry about our readiness. You know what's coming. We need the Iron Lords now more than ever." 

Saladin's eyes drifted back to the tactical display. "I know it, young pup. I'll always be here when you need me."

1820994983.name: The Summoner
1820994983.flavor: Join the dance of fire and birth.
1820994983.source_zh: 来源：奥斯里斯试炼挑战
1820994983.lore:
She awaited signal lock, hands loosely bent around flight sticks, sun to her back. Trestin's sight sank into stupor and stretched far across the outshined lights of distant possibilities. Flanking starlight pushed her jumpship's shadow outward into space. It was what it was, and nothing more.

Mercury hung beneath, buried in a storm of solar wind like a dark pit enveloped by ripe flesh. She hadn't returned in years; previous iterations of Trials and constant exposure to the Crucible had sated her curiosities of quietus. None of that mattered anymore. Not after the Moon. It was over. Finality was coming.

Trestin's return was a pretense for preparation; a living funeral to find conclusion on one's own terms. She had begun to see the sense concealed in wanton dissociation, the seriousness underneath the dressings of the Menagerie, the truth in the word ringing through its halls. It was over. Time to make peace.

"Saint-14 is going to be watching us. No pressure." Sadhij twisted a faded purple ribbon through the plates of his gauntlet and flexed his fingers.

"No pressure at all." Trestin mouthed the words, barely producing a sound before Yara's voice cut into the chatter.

"Look alive team. We are the thin line drawn before the Darkness. We are Guardians. No holding back."

Thin. A line to be swallowed in scope. No holding back.

Burning Shrine… Lock… Transmat firing…
1820994983.lore_zh:
她等待着信号锁定，双手放松地放在飞行杆上，太阳晒着她的后背。特雷斯廷的视线陷入恍惚，远远延伸到遥远的可能性的耀眼光芒之中。侧边的星光把她跃迁飞船的影子向外推入太空。就是这样，仅此而已。

水星垂在下方，埋在太阳风的风暴中，就像被腐烂的尸骨包围的黑坑一样。她已经很多年没回来了，之前的试炼迭代和不断接触熔炉竞技场，已经让她对寂灭逐渐失去了好奇心。那些事再也不重要。自从月球的事之后，再也不重要。已经结束了。终局即将到来。

特雷斯廷的回归是准备的一个借口，以自己的方式得出结论的生者葬礼。她已经开始看到在狂放的解体中隐藏着的知觉，在奇珍异兽园装扮下的严肃性，言语中的真相在大厅中响起。已经结束了。该回归平静。

“圣人14号会看着我们。不要有压力。”萨迪在他手套上缠绕着一条褪了色的紫色丝带，弯了弯手指。

“完全没有压力。”特雷斯廷说出这些话，在雅拉的声音进入聊天频道之前几乎没有发出声音。

“准备好，队员们。我们是暗影之前最后的防线。我们是守护者。绝不退缩。”

细线。将被吞噬的一道线。绝不退缩。

燃烧祭坛…锁定…传送发射…

657927352.name: Hullabaloo
657927352.lore:
Nonpareil's Ghost marks off the last of their bounties as complete, radiating satisfaction. 

Nonpareil groans. "Back home already? The energy in the Tower is so off lately." 

Behind her, Taranov shakes off her robe to release a shower of spinmetal fragments, gained on an unintended roll through the Mothyards. "Yeah, but there aren't any working showers here. Let's get going." 

"Already?" Thoughtfully, Nonpareil summons a ball of Void Light and tosses it up and down. "Hey. Taranov, think fast!" 

The other Guardian turns around just in time to catch the Light with her face. 

Taranov splutters as she's resurrected. "I will kill you." 

Nonpareil beckons to her. "Yeah? Give me your best shot." 

Taranov lifts her grenade launcher and shoots directly at Nonpareil. 

She's still bent over laughing when Nonpareil's Ghost brings her back up. 

They each go down three more times before they work out the rules for their new game: grenade launchers for the serve, Light weapons for the return. 

Nonpareil smacks the grenade firmly this time with her Sentinel Shield; Taranov watches as it sails overhead and hits an old shack in the distance. After a moment, the noise of the explosion reaches their ears. 

They keep their Ghosts busy with resurrections the whole afternoon. 

As daylight fades, so does their energy. Taranov releases her Dawnblade with a groan. "You ready to take on the Tower now?" 

Nonpareil slings an arm over her shoulder. "We're going to fix the Tower. Good times for everyone! Listen: we get in on the ground floor of a whole new sports league. Bookings. Betting. Licensed gear. The works." 

Sunset over Old Russia is a beautiful sight. Small fires burn in the scrub. The view warms Nonpareil's heart. 

A week later, they have 300 signups for their new grenadeketball league, and roughly as many citations from the Praxics for alleged manipulation of betting rings.
657927352.lore_zh:
诺帕莱尔的机灵正心满意足地把最后一个悬赏标记为完成。 

诺帕莱尔咕囔了一下。“已经要回家了？最近高塔里的气氛总有点不对。” 

在她身后，塔拉诺夫从长袍上抖落了许多掐丝金属碎片。那是她在飞蛾庭院里被迫打滚时粘上的。“是啊，但这里没有能用的淋浴。我们走吧。” 

“这么快？”诺帕莱尔若有所思，召唤出一个虚空光能球抛了起来。“嘿，塔拉诺夫，机灵点！” 

另一位守护者刚转过身，就撞上了迎面而来的光能球。 

“我要杀了你，”塔拉诺夫在复活后愤怒地说。 

诺帕莱尔向她招了招手。“是吗？放马过来。” 

塔拉诺夫举起她的榴弹发射器，直接向诺帕莱尔来了一发。 

诺帕莱尔的机灵复活她时，塔拉诺夫还笑得直不起腰。 

她们又互相将对方击杀了三次，敲定了新游戏的规则：发球者用榴弹发射器，回击者用光能武器。 

诺帕莱尔这次用哨兵圣盾狠狠地打飞了榴弹。塔拉诺夫看着榴弹击中了远处的破旧棚屋。过了一会儿，爆炸声传到了她们的耳朵里。 

她们的机灵一下午都在忙着复活她们。 

随着太阳落山，她们的精力也耗尽了。塔拉诺夫咕囔着放下了破晓。“你现在准备好挑战高塔了吗？” 

诺帕莱尔把一只手臂搭在她的肩膀上。“我们要修好高塔。大家都有好日子过！听着：我们可以主办一个全新的运动联赛。吃牌，投注，特许装备。搞全套的。” 

旧俄罗斯的日落很美。灌木丛中燃烧着小火苗。这样的景色温暖了诺帕莱尔的心。 

一周后，她们的全新榴弹联赛有三百个人报名参加，而因涉嫌操纵投注圈而被英勇教团传唤的人数也大致相同。

2372514508.name: Blast Furnace
2372514508.lore:
"…And I'll personally produce a limited number of previously unreleased designs. An alternate version of Blast Furnace, for example," Ada-1 explained. 

"First you strong-arm us into altering our specs," the VEIST rep scoffed, "And now you come begging for the very models the Vanguard rejected." 

"They would have turned the Crucible into a graveyard," Shaxx interjected. "I don't regret—" 

"I think what Lord Shaxx means to say," Ada-1 interrupted, shooting the Titan a razor-sharp glance, "is that your prototypes were ahead of market. Their time to shine is now." 

"Can the soft sell," replied the Omolon rep. "The numbers are right, so we're in." 

"But what's the catch?" the VEIST rep asked suspiciously. 

"No catch." Ada-1 steepled her fingers. "In a year's time, we'll all be dead." 

The reps shifted uncomfortably. 

"Or, we'll have defeated the Witness," she continued. "In either case, it's time to diversify our offerings. With newly released designs… and more." 

The VEIST rep arched her eyebrow. "What do you have in mind?" 

Ada's tone warmed slightly. "Just an idea. There's an old Cosmodrome program whose revival I think could be quite useful."
2372514508.lore_zh:
“…而我将亲自制作限量的，未曾发布的设计。例如，高炉的另一个版本，”艾达-1解释道。 

“你们先是强迫我们更改规格，”VEIST代表嘲笑道，“现在又来索求被先锋拒绝的那些型号。” 

“它们会把熔炉竞技场变成坟场的，”沙克斯插话道。“我不后悔——” 

“我想领主沙克斯的意思是，”艾达-1打断了他，用锐利的目光瞥了这名泰坦一眼，“你们的原型当时太过前卫。现在正是它们大放异彩的时候。” 

“软推销就省省吧，”Omolon代表答道。“数据没问题，所以我们会入伙。” 

“但是有什么花招？”VEIST代表怀疑地问道。 

“没有花招。”艾达-1并拢了手指。“一年后，我们都会死。” 

代表们不安地挪了挪身子。 

“或者，我们会击败见证者，”她接着说道。“无论是哪种情况，都是时候推进我们产品的多样化了。带来新发布的设计…以及更多东西。” 

VEIST代表抬起了眉毛。“你有什么点子？” 

艾达的语气稍微友好了些。“只是个设想。有个旧发射基地项目。我认为把它重拾起来或许会很有用。”

1896309757.name: Hammerhead
1896309757.lore:
Adit and Majjora clung to the chain link fence, well beyond the outside perimeter of the Crucible viewing area. They peered past a motionless Redjack stationed at the entrance, straining to see snippets of action on the massive viewing screens. Adit caught a glimpse of an Arc explosion as the audience roared.  

Lord Shaxx's voice boomed from the loudspeakers: "Your spirit is unrivaled. Show me more!"  

Adit glanced over at her classmate. Majjora's pinky finger was just a few centimeters away from her own, but it seemed like a kilometer. 

Adit cleared her throat, mustering courage, "So, umm, what Cryptarch Matsuo said in class today. About, like, the final shape and everything. The Witness." 

"I can't believe what I'm seeing!" Shaxx's voice rang out.  

Majjora nodded gravely. Though the visiting Cryptarch had explained the situation in the gentlest terms, the students understood the seriousness of the situation. 

"Yeah," Majjora replied. "It's… I don't know what to do." 

"Nothing we can do, I guess," Adit replied.  

Adit inched her pinky closer to Majjora's for what felt like an eternity. And then finally, they touched.  

Majjora smiled.  

A Stasis grenade detonated on the viewing screens, but neither of them heard it.
1896309757.lore_zh:
阿迪特和玛乔拉紧紧地抓着远在熔炉竞技场观战区之外的链条栅栏。她们的目光越过入口处静止不动的红桃杰克，费劲想要看到巨型观赏屏幕上的动作片段。阿迪特瞥见一股电弧爆炸，观众们随之沸腾。  

扩音器中传出了领主沙克斯的洪亮声音：“你的热情无人能敌。再多给我看看！”  

阿迪特瞥了一眼她的同学。玛乔拉的小指离她的小指只有几厘米远，但却仿佛有一公里之遥。 

阿迪特清了清嗓子，鼓起勇气，“对了，唔，解密大师松尾今天在课堂上说的话。关于终焉之形什么的。还有见证者。” 

“我简直不敢相信眼前的这一切！”沙克斯的声音响了起来。  

玛乔拉严肃地点了点头。虽然到访的解密大师用最温和的言辞去解释现状，但学生们都明白事态的严重性。 

“是啊，”玛乔拉答道。“我…我不知道该怎么做。” 

“我猜我们什么也做不了，”阿迪特答道。  

阿迪特的小指靠近了玛乔拉的小指，感觉像是过了很久。最后，它们终于碰到了一起。  

玛乔拉露出了微笑。  

一枚冰影手雷在观赏屏幕上爆炸，但她们都没有听见。

568611923.name: Edge Transit
568611923.flavor: What did you trade away to secure passage to the edge?
568611923.lore:
Devrim was surrounded as soon as he arrived in Neu Turbach. Villagers patted him on the arms, children tugged at his fatigues, and homemade treats were stuffed into his pockets. Each one thanked him in their own way. 

Eventually the village leader, Joacham, led him to a small homestead. A spread of tea and sweet pastries were laid out. Devrim was honored—tea and sugar were rare commodities this far from the City. 

"We expect another offensive in the coming weeks," Devrim advised. "We suggest you start preparing immediately." 

Joacham grinned. "We have been preparing ever since the last attack. We now have trip wires, barricades, and even an auto turret!" 

Devrim's chest swelled with pride. It was not long ago that he'd taught these same villagers to defend themselves against Shadow Legion captors. At the time, he'd wondered whether they would last the winter. Now, they were stronger than ever. 

"Would you like to see the upgrades?" Joacham offered. 

Devrim beamed. "Nothing would make me happier."
568611923.lore_zh:
德弗里姆一到纽图尔巴赫就被团团围住。村民们拍他的胳膊，孩子们拽他的军装，还有人把自制零食塞进他的口袋。每个人都用自己的方式向他表示感谢。 

最后，村长乔查姆把他领到一个小宅院。那里摆满了茶和甜点。德弗里姆感到很荣幸——茶和糖在离圣城这么远的地方可是稀罕物。 

“我们预测未来几周还会有一次进攻，”德弗里姆提出。“我们建议你们立即开始准备。” 

乔查姆咧嘴一笑。“我们自从上次袭击以来就一直在准备。我们现在有拌线、屏障，甚至还有自动炮台！” 

德弗里姆胸中涌起一股自豪感。不久前他还在教这些村民如何避免成为暗影军团的俘虏。当时，他甚至不知道他们能否撑过那个冬天。现在，他们比以往任何时候都更加强大。 

“你想看看我们的升级吗？”乔查姆提议道。 

德弗里姆露出了笑容。“我求之不得。”

2763843899.name: Luna's Howl
2763843899.flavor: "Guardians never die. But we don't forget those who do." —Lord Shaxx
2763843899.lore:
Josef opened the door. Shaxx filled the hallway beyond. 

"You look tired," said the Crucible handler. "But I have just the thing to get you buzzing." 

"No time for the Crucible," Josef dissembled. "Another day." 

"I'll hold you to that. But that's not what I meant." 

Josef said nothing. 

"I was speaking with Saladin," Shaxx continued. "We were remembering all the people we left behind over the years. Your name came up." 

"Oh yeah?" 

Shaxx held out a cardboard box, perforated with large holes. "The Valus asked me to deliver this." 

Josef opened the box. At the bottom, in a nest of cloud accretions, were two sleeping war beast pups. 

"They're not replacements," Shaxx explained, "but we hope they bring some light back into your life." 

"They're perfect," Josef said, his voice tender. "Thank you." 

"See them settled. Then I expect you back in the Crucible to teach MY pups a thing or two."
2763843899.lore_zh:
约瑟夫打开了门。沙克斯巨大的身躯占满了走廊。 

“你看起来很疲惫，”这名熔炉竞技场顾问说道。“但我有个东西能让你提起劲来。” 

“我没时间参加熔炉竞技场，”约瑟夫敷衍道。“改天吧。” 

“那你可要说话算数。不过，你误解了我刚才说的话。” 

约瑟夫没有作声。 

“我之前跟萨拉丁聊了下，”沙克斯继续说道。“我们回忆了这些年来淡出视野的人。我们提起了你的名字。” 

“哦，是吗？” 

沙克斯拿出一个纸箱，上面有很多大洞。“军政官让我把这个交给你。” 

约瑟夫打开了箱子。在其底部的云端积层里有两只熟睡的战兽幼崽。 

“它们不是替代品，”沙克斯解释道，“但我们希望它们能给你的生活带回一些光明。” 

“它们很棒，”约瑟夫温柔地说。“谢谢你们。” 

“好好安顿它们。然后，我希望你能回到熔炉竞技场里，教教我的那些幼崽。”
