1006498763.name: Star-Eater Scales
1006498763.flavor: Feast on the sky. Gorge yourself until all starlight has been gnawed to black—then the cosmos will tremble with your roar.
1006498763.lore:
The harsh buzz of a sawtooth wave jolted Ekris from slumber. He groaned, slid off his cot, and slumped into the pilot's chair. Large amounts of data streamed across an array of thick glass screens while the alarm blared. He connected all the various details: heavy interference on scanners, propulsion malfunction in the main drive, erroneous flags on the proximity detectors. He looked through the porthole, a glass circle no more than five inches wide, and saw wisps of blue particulates wash past.

"Collision?" he pondered.

A voice called out behind him. "Still days out from the belt, nothing here to hit."

Ekris pivoted around and saw his copilot. He squinted, trying to remember the other Eliksni's name, but nothing came to him. He felt bad about that. They'd been in transit awhile and he still couldn't remember this one's name.

"It's Raksil," the copilot said as he focused on the instrument displays. "You make that face every time you forget my name."

Ekris looked away in shame. "Strange coincidence. Had a brother Raksil."

"There are many Raksil-brothers and Ekris-pilots, if you look far enough," the copilot said.

Ekris wasn't convinced that was true, but it wasn't important.

"Drive is down," Ekris said. "Stuck in a field of something."

"Not stuck," Raksil said as he punched in some commands through the dash controls, stopping the alarm. "Just slow. Velocity steady."

"No control…" Ekris chittered nervously. "If we're lucky, we'll drift out eventually."

"Long road just to get to Misraaks." Raksil sat on the bulkhead and sighed. "You still think he's Kell of Kells?"

Ekris' mind buzzed with an odd sensation. He didn't remember sharing that with his copilot.

"Best chance I've seen," he said. "He is different, brings us together in new ways."

Raksil made a click with his mandible. "Heard that before."

Ekris waved his claw dismissively. "You always dissent, just to be a dissenter."

"I want to free you from this obsession," Raksil replied.

Ekris scoffed. "Kell of Kells is a symbol of hope for all Eliksni. You would rather we live without that?"

"This myth divides us, brother," Raksil said. "We rend and tear, trying to claw our way to the top of the mountain. Then we look down and see the mountain is made of our torn banners."

Something itched in Ekris's mind. Did Raksil just call him "brother"?

Raksil continued his thought. "The only unity down this path is collective death. The Kell of Kells is destined to rule only the House of Silence."

Ekris clicked his jaw angrily. "Why would Eliksni dream of this Kell, if the dream only harms us?"

"Maybe we didn't," Raksil said with a devilish grin. "Maybe something else dreamt it for us. To keep us apart."

Ekris waved his claws and stood, pacing around the cabin. "Enough. You are stretched thin by this journey; you need more sleep—go to your bunk." His mind itched again. There was only one cot in the ship. He stumbled as the dizziness overcame his senses. When he looked up, he was alone.

"You've chased this dream so long you've forgotten you're asleep," Raksil said, a hint of mourning in his voice—the sound came from nowhere in particular. The pilot's console was dim and quiet. The instrument readouts had slowed and showed no warnings. Ekris looked toward the porthole and saw nothing but black, peppered with the sparse glimmer of distant stars.
1006498763.lore_zh:
锯齿波刺耳的嗡嗡声把埃克里斯从睡梦中惊醒。他哼哼唧唧地从折叠床上滑落下来，一屁股坐在飞行员座椅上。伴随着警报声，大量数据在一排厚玻璃屏幕上滚动显示。他把所有不同细节都汇总了一下：扫描器受到严重干扰、主驱动器存在推进故障、接近探测器上的错误标记。他透过舷窗（一个不超过五英寸宽的玻璃圆窗）看到一缕缕的蓝色微粒正在飘过。

“发生了撞击吗？”他思索着。

他身后传来了一个声音。“还要几天才能到行星带，这里没东西可撞。”

埃克里斯转过身看了看他的副驾驶员。他眯起眼睛，试图回想起这个埃里克斯尼族的名字，但却想不起来。他为此感到歉疚。他们已经航行一阵子了，但他还是记不住这家伙的名字。

“我叫拉克索，”副驾驶员一边专注地查看仪表显示，一边说道。“每次你忘记我的名字时，脸上总是那副表情。”

埃克里斯羞愧地扭过头去。“真是个奇怪的巧合。我有个兄弟就叫拉克索。”

“如果你阅历足够，就会认识很多拉克索兄弟和埃克里斯驾驶员，”副驾驶员说道。

埃克里斯不相信那是真的，但这并不重要。

“驱动器停止工作了，”埃克里斯说道。“我们被困在了某种东西的里面。”

“没有被困住，”拉克索一边说着，一边通过仪表板控制器输入指令取消了警报。“只是很慢。飞行速度很稳定。”

“控制装置失效了…”埃克里斯紧张地唠叨起来。“如果我们走运的话，最后会成功地飘出去吧。”

“单是与米斯拉阿克斯汇合，就还有很长的路要走。”拉克索坐在舱壁上叹了口气。“你仍然认为他是凯尔之王吗？”

埃克里斯的头脑中涌现出一种奇怪的感觉。他不记得和他的副驾驶员说过这事。

“我觉得极有可能，”他说道。“他与众不同，用全新方式把我们团结在了一起。”

拉克索啧了一下嘴。“这话你以前说过。”

埃克里斯不屑一顾地挥了挥爪子。“你总是跟我抬杠，为了抬杠而抬杠。”

“我想把你从这种痴迷中拯救出来，”拉克索回答道。

埃克里斯嗤之以鼻。“对所有埃里克斯尼族来说，凯尔之王是希望的象征。你难道宁愿我们毫无希望地活下去？”

“这个迷思使我们产生了分歧，兄弟，”拉克索说道。“我们不断撕扯，努力爬上山顶。然后我们从山顶往下看，望见整座山上布满了被我们撕烂的旗帜。”

埃克里斯的心里咯噔了一下。拉克索刚才叫他“兄弟”？

拉克索继续说着他的想法。“沿着这条路走下去，唯一能达成的统一就是集体死亡。凯尔之王注定只能统治静默氏族。”

埃克里斯生气地咬起了牙。“如果这个梦只会伤害我们，那为什么埃里克斯尼族会梦见这个凯尔？”

“也许我们并没有梦见他，”拉克索邪笑着说道。“也许这个梦是被强加的。好让我们产生分歧。”

埃克里斯挥了挥爪子，站起来在驾驶舱内来回踱步。“够了。这次的旅行把你累坏了；你需要更多睡眠，回你的床铺吧。”他的心里又咯噔了一下。飞船里只有一个折叠床。他感到头晕目眩，踉跄了一下。当他抬头看的时候，周围别无他人。

“你追逐这个梦想太久，以至于忘记了自己是在睡觉，”拉克索说道。他的声音里带着一丝哀伤，不知是从哪里传来的。驾驶员控制台昏暗而又安静。仪表的读数显示慢了下来，没有任何警报。埃克里斯朝着舷窗看去，窗外只有一片漆黑，点缀着遥远恒星的零星微光。

1538369423.name: Star-Eater Scales
1538369423.flavor: Feast on the sky. Gorge yourself until all starlight has been gnawed to black—then the cosmos will tremble with your roar.
1538369423.lore:
The harsh buzz of a sawtooth wave jolted Ekris from slumber. He groaned, slid off his cot, and slumped into the pilot's chair. Large amounts of data streamed across an array of thick glass screens while the alarm blared. He connected all the various details: heavy interference on scanners, propulsion malfunction in the main drive, erroneous flags on the proximity detectors. He looked through the porthole, a glass circle no more than five inches wide, and saw wisps of blue particulates wash past.

"Collision?" he pondered.

A voice called out behind him. "Still days out from the belt, nothing here to hit."

Ekris pivoted around and saw his copilot. He squinted, trying to remember the other Eliksni's name, but nothing came to him. He felt bad about that. They'd been in transit awhile and he still couldn't remember this one's name.

"It's Raksil," the copilot said as he focused on the instrument displays. "You make that face every time you forget my name."

Ekris looked away in shame. "Strange coincidence. Had a brother Raksil."

"There are many Raksil-brothers and Ekris-pilots, if you look far enough," the copilot said.

Ekris wasn't convinced that was true, but it wasn't important.

"Drive is down," Ekris said. "Stuck in a field of something."

"Not stuck," Raksil said as he punched in some commands through the dash controls, stopping the alarm. "Just slow. Velocity steady."

"No control…" Ekris chittered nervously. "If we're lucky, we'll drift out eventually."

"Long road just to get to Misraaks." Raksil sat on the bulkhead and sighed. "You still think he's Kell of Kells?"

Ekris' mind buzzed with an odd sensation. He didn't remember sharing that with his copilot.

"Best chance I've seen," he said. "He is different, brings us together in new ways."

Raksil made a click with his mandible. "Heard that before."

Ekris waved his claw dismissively. "You always dissent, just to be a dissenter."

"I want to free you from this obsession," Raksil replied.

Ekris scoffed. "Kell of Kells is a symbol of hope for all Eliksni. You would rather we live without that?"

"This myth divides us, brother," Raksil said. "We rend and tear, trying to claw our way to the top of the mountain. Then we look down and see the mountain is made of our torn banners."

Something itched in Ekris's mind. Did Raksil just call him "brother"?

Raksil continued his thought. "The only unity down this path is collective death. The Kell of Kells is destined to rule only the House of Silence."

Ekris clicked his jaw angrily. "Why would Eliksni dream of this Kell, if the dream only harms us?"

"Maybe we didn't," Raksil said with a devilish grin. "Maybe something else dreamt it for us. To keep us apart."

Ekris waved his claws and stood, pacing around the cabin. "Enough. You are stretched thin by this journey; you need more sleep—go to your bunk." His mind itched again. There was only one cot in the ship. He stumbled as the dizziness overcame his senses. When he looked up, he was alone.

"You've chased this dream so long you've forgotten you're asleep," Raksil said, a hint of mourning in his voice—the sound came from nowhere in particular. The pilot's console was dim and quiet. The instrument readouts had slowed and showed no warnings. Ekris looked toward the porthole and saw nothing but black, peppered with the sparse glimmer of distant stars.

3793245444.name: Renewal Grasps
3793245444.lore:
"Regrettably, Lakshmi was killed by Vex during the assault…" 

Ikora's words echoed like the tolling of a bell. Ada-1 rocked back on her heels. She had never much liked Lakshmi-2—tolerated was a better word—but her fellow Exo had been her partner in a very intriguing new venture. Now, Lakshmi was dead, and so was the promise of Project Stronghold. 

A bunker where the city's leaders could be preserved through any attack was now just a hazy memory. Project Stronghold's reach was more expansive than Ada's contribution. Indeed, her focus had been steered in this direction by Lakshmi, yet the necessity of the bunker had made perfect sense when Lakshmi proposed the endeavor. A city cannot survive without its leaders, but Ada never expected that Lakshmi herself would instigate an attack. 

Ada-1 had been used. The realization stung, but having yet another venture collapse around her was too bitter a pill to swallow. She was destined for greatness, wasn't she? 

Ada heard the servos in her hands whining. Her fists were balled tight. She hadn't meant to… she hadn't meant for any of this. Every day spent, every breakthrough made, just grains of sand in a sculpture doomed to be washed away by the unstoppable tide. 

She had worked for years to defend this system, its people; and all she had to show for it was a glorified spindle. 

No matter. For now, she would focus on one day at a time, and today, she would spin gold from straw. Her fingers traced the lines on the shoulder of the new gauntlets she had designed. She was determined to see them completed. They wouldn't save the system, no, but they would represent the Black Armory well. Sometimes, she just needed something for herself.
3793245444.lore_zh:
“遗憾的是，拉克希米在袭击中被Vex所杀害…” 

艾可拉所说的话如钟声一般回响。艾达-1感到十分震惊，她从来就不怎么喜欢（也许“容忍”比较贴切）拉克希米-2，但她的同伴Exo曾是她有趣冒险旅程中的伙伴。拉克希米死了，据点计划的承诺也随着她烟消云散。 

一个在受到攻击时保护圣城领导的地堡现在只是个模糊的记忆。据点计划的范畴比艾达所贡献的还要广阔。当然，她的重点被拉克希米引导至此，但地堡的重要性在拉克希米提出计划时是非常合理的。圣城无法在没有领导的情况下生存下去，但艾达从未想过拉克希米本身会先发起进攻。 

艾达-1被利用了，这个认知让人震惊。但眼见又一个项目在她周围崩溃是一颗难以下咽的苦果。她注定要成就一番事业的，不是吗？ 

艾达听到她手中的伺服零件在呜呜作响。她攥紧了拳头，她不是有意的…这一切都并不是她的本意。度过的每一天，每一次的突破，都只是雕塑中注定要被势不可挡的潮水冲走的渺小沙粒。 

多年来，她一直在努力捍卫这个星系，捍卫生活在其中的人们，而她所能展示的，只是这个美化了的纺锤。 

不管怎样，现在，她会专注于每一天，而今天，她甚至会把稻草纺成金子。她用手指描绘着她设计的新臂铠肩部的纹路。她要亲眼看着它们完成。这套护臂虽然无法拯救星系，但它们充分代表了黑色军武，有时她只是想为自己做点什么。

863908533.name: Blight Ranger
863908533.flavor: It reflects whatever it sees, no matter how ugly.
863908533.lore:
I've thanked God for this mask more times than I can count. It reflects most everything; keeps me on the safe side of whatever's coming at me. Most times…

Dust storm left me no recourse. Came to a small encampment of refugees from Freehold, now buried. Most of them were workers at the old BrayTech facility, none too happy to see an Exo. One of them began to play a rueful tune on a cobbled-together string instrument. To this day, I haven't forgotten the words he sang:

Let me tell ya now 
Bout the time the Devil walked through my door
Said oh, let me tell ya now
Bout the time the Devil walked through that door
Ain't nothin', nobody
Could hold me down anymore

It was mine, all mine
Devil gave me that golden ring
It was mine, all mine
Devil made me laugh and sing
But little by little
The Devil took my everything

It was wailin' and gnashin'
When the Devil did his dirty work
Just wailin' and gnashin'
When the Devil did his dirty work
Oh, what a fool had I been
Thinkin' I was above the dirt

In the dirt, they were buried
Made me blue to see that red
In the dirt, they were buried
Made me blue to see that red
Devil took no pity
Left me no place to rest my head

Lord, help the Devil
How'd he get to be so cruel
Lord, help that Devil
How'd he get to be so cruel
That mean old Devil
Was just some other devil's fool

This mask reflected the gaunt faces of the survivors, but it didn't hide me. I could feel hot tears stream down my cheeks. They saw their own pain in me. The accusatory glances stopped then, and a sad understanding remained. Because we all knew, this place will never be the same.
863908533.lore_zh:
我曾无数次感谢上帝赐予我这副面具。它几乎能反弹一切，让我在面对任何威胁时都能受到保护。大多数时候吧…

沙尘暴使我无法求援，我来到了自由地带的一个小难民营，不过现已被埋了。他们中的大多数人都是老布瑞科技工厂的工人，特别对Exo反感。其中一人开始用一个自制的简易弦乐器奏出悲伤的曲调。直到今天我仍无法忘记他唱的歌词：

让我现在给你讲个故事 
关于一个恶魔走进我的大门的故事
哦，让我现在给你讲个故事
关于一个恶魔走进我的大门的故事
没有任何东西，也没人
能够阻止我

它是我的，全都属于我
恶魔给了我那枚金戒指
它是我的，全都属于我
恶魔让我又笑又唱
但渐渐地
恶魔夺走了我的一切

哀嚎四起，咬牙切齿
恶魔开始捣乱了
哀嚎四起，咬牙切齿
恶魔开始捣乱了
哦，我真是个傻瓜
以为自己在泥土之上

在他们被埋的泥土里
看到那抹红使我忧伤
在他们被埋的泥土里
看到那抹红使我忧伤
那个恶魔不知怜悯
一点也不让休息

上帝啊，帮帮这个恶魔吧
他怎么变得这么残忍
上帝啊，帮帮这个恶魔吧
他怎么变得这么残忍
那个刻薄的老恶魔
不过是其他恶魔的傻瓜

这个面具映照出幸存者憔悴的面孔，但没有隐藏起我的面孔。我能感觉到滚烫的眼泪顺着脸颊流下来。他们在我身上看到了他们自己的痛苦。他们不再投来指责的目光，只剩下一种悲痛的同理心。因为我们都知道，这个地方将永远也恢复不到原来的样子了。

沙尘暴使我无法求援，我来到了自由地带的一个小难民营，不过现已被埋了。他们中的大多数人都是老布瑞科技工厂的工人，特别对Exo反感。其中一人开始用一个自制的简易弦乐器奏出悲伤的曲调。直到今天我仍无法忘记他唱的歌词：

让我现在给你讲个故事 
关于一个恶魔走进我的大门的故事
哦，让我现在给你讲个故事
关于一个恶魔走进我的大门的故事
没有任何东西，也没人
能够阻止我

它是我的，全都属于我
恶魔给了我那枚金戒指
它是我的，全都属于我
恶魔让我又笑又唱
但渐渐地
恶魔夺走了我的一切

哀嚎四起，咬牙切齿
恶魔开始捣乱了
哀嚎四起，咬牙切齿
恶魔开始捣乱了
哦，我真是个傻瓜
以为自己在泥土之上

在他们被埋的泥土里
看到那抹红使我忧伤
在他们被埋的泥土里
看到那抹红使我忧伤
那个恶魔不知怜悯
一点也不让休息

上帝啊，帮帮这个恶魔吧
他怎么变得这么残忍
上帝啊，帮帮这个恶魔吧
他怎么变得这么残忍
那个刻薄的老恶魔
不过是其他恶魔的傻瓜

这个面具映照出幸存者憔悴的面孔，但没有隐藏起我的面孔。我能感觉到滚烫的眼泪顺着脸颊流下来。他们在我身上看到了他们自己的痛苦。他们不再投来指责的目光，只剩下一种悲痛的同理心。因为我们都知道，这个地方将永远也恢复不到原来的样子了。

327385975.name: Caliban's Hand
327385975.flavor: Always keep one up your sleeve.
327385975.lore:
Caliban-8 had the singular misfortune of "winning" the position of Hunter Vanguard in a card game he didn't even play. All he'd done was deal the hand that lost Tallulah Fairwind's bet—and her life—to an Ahamkara.

Not a day went by where he didn't wish he'd cheated. At least then, the wish-dragon might have killed him as well.

Now he sat as the second Hunter Vanguard in the City's history, chained to a desk in the Tower. Responsible for a breed of Guardians notorious for their unwillingness to answer communications or follow directions. Lulah knew how to inspire a sense of camaraderie in them. But Caliban?

He was just a guy who dealt the wrong hand.

Leaning back in his chair, he flipped a Light-heated knife between his fingers and tossed it up into the ceiling. Its molten edge slid into the steel and instantly cooled, stuck alongside the other half dozen blades he'd previously used to deface his office. 

It had been a slow afternoon.

A light knock on his door caught his attention. An unassuming figure, robed and masked in white, stood at the entrance to the room.

"Hard at work, I see," remarked the Speaker.

Caliban scoffed as he got to his feet. "Not sure what you expect me to do from behind a desk. You know how Hunters are."

The Speaker nodded, then looked up to the ceiling. "How many knives do you have up your sleeve, Caliban?"

"About that many," he joked, pointing upward.

"Then it seems you must get up and collect them," the Speaker mused. "Much like your Hunters."

Caliban began to reply, but for once, he didn't know what to say. The Speaker turned from the doorway and called out over his shoulder. 

"Take your time, Caliban. The desk will be here still when you return."
327385975.lore_zh:
卡利班-8非常不幸地在一场他甚至没有玩的纸牌游戏里“赢得”了猎人先锋的位置。他所做的只是打出了将塔鲁·和风的赌注——还有她的性命——输给阿罕卡拉的一手牌。

他无时无刻都希望自己当时做了老千。至少那样，神龙就会把他也杀了。

如今他坐在圣城历史第二个猎人先锋的位子上，被锁在高塔里的一张桌子上。负责一批因不愿回应通讯或听从指示而臭名远扬的守护者。鲁拉知道如何激发他们的同志情谊。但是卡利班呢？

他只是一个打错了牌的家伙。

他向后靠在椅子上，用手指翻起一把光能加热的飞刀，朝天花板扔去。它灼热的刀刃滑入钢中瞬间冷却，插在他之前用来毁坏他办公室的其他半打刀片的旁边。 

这真是个漫长的下午。

轻轻的敲门声引起了他的注意。一个穿着白袍，戴着白色面具的谦逊人物站在房间的入口处。

“看得出来，你工作得很卖力，”先知评论道。

卡利班站起身来嘲笑道。“我不知道你想让我在一张办公桌后面做什么。你知道猎人是什么样的。”

先知点点头，然后抬头看着天花板。“你袖子里有多少把飞刀，卡利班？”

“大概这么多，”他开玩笑地朝上指了指。

“那看来你必须站起身去取回它们，”先知沉思道。“就像你其他的猎人同伴一样。”

卡利班想开口回答，但这一次，他不知道要说什么。先知从门口转过身来，回过头喊道。 

“慢慢来，卡利班。等你回来的时候，桌子还会在这。”

2447096246.name: Gyrfalcon's Hauberk
2447096246.flavor: The higher your flight, the faster your dive.
2447096246.lore:
"What's that?"

It's a childish question, really.

"There it is again! Did you hear it?"

That's more like it.

"No…"

Of course you didn't.

"Do you see something?"

Of course they don't.

"No."

I'm just a trick of the eye.

"It's probably nothing."

That's right.

"Yeah. It's nothing."

They won't see me coming.
2447096246.lore_zh:
“那是什么？”

真是个幼稚的问题。

“又来了！你听见了吗？”

这才像话嘛。

“没…”

当然没有。

“你看见什么了吗？”

当然没有。

“没。”

我只是眼睛的错觉。

“是我想多了吧。”

没错。

“对。你想多了。”

他们发现不了我。

1008364980.name: Cyrtarachne's Facade
1008364980.lore:
Dumpster diving wasn't the classiest of hobbies, but it gave her insight she couldn't get anywhere else. At least, that's what she reminded her Ghost as the two scoured the alleyways of Neomuna.

The helmet had a lovely heft in her hands as she pulled it from a pile of expired tech and half-melted Vex. This was a rare find. Turns out people who live in a highly advanced virtual society also have an almost perfect waste disposal system. Almost.

As she examined her prize, she spied something poking out from inside. She retrieved five yellowed sheets of actual paper, covered in barely legible writing:

Expedition #17: Thalassa. Unsatisfied with excursions on Neptune, I've begun to take my trips a bit further to its surrounding moons—

Boring, she skipped ahead.

—appears to be a conglomeration of space junk long fused together. Deep blue, green, and yellow hues ripple across amalgamate hills—

Too many big words.

—I do not appear to be its first visitor—

She continued to skim.

—ship wreckage—

—old pieces of armor, coloring unlike anything I've ever seen—

—not made for a Human—

Huh. The helm sure looked like it would fit.

—large creatures, MANY legs—

Her eyes widened. Finally, it was getting good. She turned the page over… nothing. Blank. 

With a scoff, she crumpled up the papers, tossed them over her shoulder, and stalked off with the helmet.

Expedition Log #17: 

Neptune's Second Closest Satellite, Thalassa: Neptune's wilderness proved unsatisfying, so I've begun to take trips further out to surrounding moons. Equipment detected several chemical signatures; samples should be plentiful. If readings are accurate, collected resources will help Neomuna greatly.

Touchdown Evaluation: Initial readings detect nominal quantities of phosphates and bountiful networks of framework silicates. Networks are jutting out from nearby caverns and visible to the naked eye. 

I cite novice oil painting skills to describe the networks' hues as such: deep blue, green, and yellow. [NOTE: cross-reference hue interpretation with paint tubes]. 

I cite minimal creative writing knowledge to describe the landscape: the hues ripple across amalgamate hills that roll as far as the eye can see. 

Initial Exploration: Came upon a shipwreck, very old, parts burnt out beyond recognition. Found items in nearby area:

- 1 armored glove: unusable, built for three digits, one of which appears opposable

- 2 armored shin guards: simple design, both cracked

- 1 helmet: visor intact

Observations: The armor is painted. Markings unrecognizable but appear intentional. 

Hazard[!]: Fauna observed at nearest cavern—large creatures, MANY legs, pincers. Having no experience in zoology, I conclude: probably unfriendly. Discovered the unique pattern on the found helmet matches the coloring of the creatures. n attempted disguise?

Sample Collected: framework silicate, 2.2 kilos.

Continued Observation: Creatures are unfriendly. Attempted to collect more samples, unknowingly encroached on territory. 

Theory: Helmet was indeed an attempted disguise, perhaps I will utilize it as well.

[End documentation]
1008364980.lore_zh:
翻垃圾箱并不是最时髦的爱好，但它能让她获得她在其他任何地方都得不到的认知。至少，当他们在内欧姆那的小巷里搜寻时，她是这样提醒她的机灵的。

她从一堆过期科技和半融化的Vex中拽出它时，那头盔在她手中显得小巧可爱。这可是个难得的发现。事实证明，生活在高度发达的虚拟社会中的人也有一个近乎完美的废物处理系统。近乎完美。

在检视自己的奖品时，她发现有什么东西从里面露了出来。她找到了五张泛黄的实体纸片，上面写着难以辨认的字迹：

第17次远征：海卫四。由于不满足于海王星上的短途旅行，我开始到更远的地方去看看它周围的卫星…

有点无聊，她略过了一些内容。

…似乎是一堆长期凝聚在一起的太空垃圾。深蓝色、绿色和黄色的色调在混合的山丘上起伏…

太多难懂的词汇了。

…我似乎不是它的第一位访客…

她继续略读着。

…飞船残骸…

…旧护甲碎片，着色和我所见过的任何东西都不一样…

…不是为人类而造的…

哈。这头盔看起来倒是挺合适。

…大型生物，有多条腿…

她睁大了眼睛。终于，内容开始有趣了。她把纸页翻过来…什么也没有。一片空白。 

她嘲弄地笑了笑，把纸片揉成一团，甩过肩后，带着头盔扬长而去。

远征日志#17： 

海王星第二近的卫星，海卫四：海王星的荒野不尽如人意，所以我开始前往更远的地方：周围的卫星。设备检测到多种化学信号；样本应该相当充足。如果读数准确的话，采集到的资源将对内欧姆那大有帮助。

触地评估：初始读数检测到标称量的磷酸盐和丰富的架状硅酸盐网簇。网簇从附近洞穴中突出，肉眼可见。 

我引用初级的油画技巧来描述网簇的色彩：深蓝色、绿色和黄色。[注：使用涂料管进行比对色彩阐释]。 

我引用极少的创意写作知识来描述眼前的景象：混合的山丘间荡漾的色彩一望无际。 

初步探索：发现了一艘沉船，非常古老，零部件已烧得面目全非。在附近地区发现的物品有：

- 1只装甲手套：无法使用，专为三根手指而造，其中一根似乎与其他手指相对

- 2件装甲护胫：设计简单，都有裂缝

- 1个头盔：面罩完好无损

观察：护甲上有喷漆。印记已无法辨认，但似乎是有意的。 

危险[!]：在最近的洞穴中观察到的动物群——大型生物，有多条腿，带有钳肢。虽然没有动物学经验，我还是得出结论：大概率不友好。发现找到的头盔上的独特图案与这些生物的颜色相吻合。是想要伪装？

采集到的样本：架状硅酸盐，2.2公斤。

继续观察：这些生物不友好。试图采集更多的样本时，不知不觉侵占了领土。 

理论：头盔确实是一种伪装，也许我也会加以利用。

[文档结束]

我引用初级的油画技巧来描述网簇的色彩：深蓝色、绿色和黄色。[注：使用涂料管进行比对色彩阐释]。 

我引用极少的创意写作知识来描述眼前的景象：混合的山丘间荡漾的色彩一望无际。 

初步探索：发现了一艘沉船，非常古老，零部件已烧得面目全非。在附近地区发现的物品有：

- 1只装甲手套：无法使用，专为三根手指而造，其中一根似乎与其他手指相对

- 2件装甲护胫：设计简单，都有裂缝

- 1个头盔：面罩完好无损

观察：护甲上有喷漆。印记已无法辨认，但似乎是有意的。 

危险[!]：在最近的洞穴中观察到的动物群——大型生物，有多条腿，带有钳肢。虽然没有动物学经验，我还是得出结论：大概率不友好。发现找到的头盔上的独特图案与这些生物的颜色相吻合。是想要伪装？

采集到的样本：架状硅酸盐，2.2公斤。

继续观察：这些生物不友好。试图采集更多的样本时，不知不觉侵占了领土。 

理论：头盔确实是一种伪装，也许我也会加以利用。

[文档结束]

1304266146.name: Triton Vice
1304266146.lore:
"What… are you wearing?"  

"These are the grasping pincers of Titan's apex predator! Replicated in miniature, of course. I'm sure the real thing would tower over us."  

"I've read Pahanin's treatise on cephalopods—"  

"No, not squids. Crabs, obviously! The perfect organism! The form toward which all life inevitably converges! Even on Nessus—" 

"Those are not crabs. Where are you getting all this?" 

"The VanNet. Look, the farther out from Earth we get, the more we'll see that crabs are everywhere. Look at the Eliksni!" 

"The Eliksni don't have a common ancestor with anything on Earth, so I don't think our taxonomy really applies to the—" 

"How big do you think an Eliksni can get? Do you think there's a giant one out there somewhere? …I'm asking Variks."  

"Do NOT ask—hey, come back!"
1304266146.lore_zh:
“你…你这戴的是什么？”  

“这些是土卫六顶级掠食者的钳取螯足！当然是微型复制品啦。我敢肯定真正的个体远比我们高大。”  

“我读过帕汉宁关于头足类动物的论文——”  

“不，不是鱿鱼。很显然，是螃蟹！完美的生物！所有生命都不可避免趋同的形式！就连涅索斯上——” 

“那些可不是螃蟹。你从哪儿弄到这些的？” 

“从VanNet上。听着，我们离地球越远，就越会发现螃蟹无处不在。看看埃里克斯尼族！” 

“埃里克斯尼族和地球上的任何生物都没有共同祖先，所以我认为我们的分类法并不适用于——” 

“你觉得一个埃里克斯尼族能长成多大？你觉得在某个地方会有个无比巨大的家伙么？…我去问问瓦里克斯。”  

“别问——喂，回来！”

3688534631.name: Mothkeeper's Wraps
3688534631.lore:
She had tracked the infested Ogre across the Throne World, led by its trailing effluvium. Now it lay collapsed against a cracked jade pillar, its wheezing form obscured by a thick blanket of moths. 

As she approached, ripples of startling color shimmered over the Ogre as the moths flashed their vibrant underwings in warning. She pulled her hood tight against her exposed face. She would have to work quickly.

The moths on the ground shivered as she stepped carefully over them. She took a breath of the powdery air and reached into the rustling mass, shoulder deep, as quivering wings beat against her neck. She groped blindly until her fingers finally grazed against the withered Ogre, its hide yielding as old leather.

Her knife was swift and sure. The Ogre shuddered once, and it was over. As she withdrew her blade, the moths took flight with the muffled rush of a thousand zephyr-borne petals.

Then they were upon her, covering her cloak, her shoulders, landing in her hair. They smothered her with their dusty bodies, brushing against her lips as she whispered the incantation she stole from the Witch Queen's Spire. She traced the outline of a Hive rune in the air with her knife, then touched the tip of the blade to the back of her hand.

The moths fell still, hushed, bipectinate antennae quivering as they considered the offer:

Not a host, but a home.
3688534631.lore_zh:
她在王座世界里追踪那个受到感染的虫瘤，寻找它身后的恶臭。现在它瘫倒在一根裂开的玉柱上，大口喘息的身影被一层厚厚的飞蛾遮住。 

她走近过去，虫瘤的头顶上闪烁着不寻常的色彩涟漪，那是飞蛾在扑闪着它们充满活力的翅膀以示警告。她把兜帽拉向露在外面的脸庞前，贴得紧紧的。她必须动作快点。

地面上的飞蛾在她小心翼翼地跨过时害怕地颤抖着。她吸了一口满是蛾粉的空气，把手伸到齐肩深、沙沙作响的蛾群中，颤动的翅膀拍打着她的脖子。她盲目地摸索着，直到触及了那个衰弱虫瘤。它的表皮就像旧皮革一样柔软。

她的刀又快又准。虫瘤颤抖了一下，一切就结束了。她拔出刀刃，蛾群带着万千和风花瓣的闷响飞了起来。

然后它们飞到她身上，遮盖她的披风，她的肩膀，落在她的头发上。它们用满是蛾粉的身体让她窒息，在她低声念着从巫妖女王的尖塔上偷来的咒语时拂过她的嘴唇。她用刀刃在空中勾勒出邪魔族符文的轮廓，然后用刀尖碰了碰手背。

飞蛾们安静缄默地落下，双栉形的触须颤抖着，思忖着这个提议：

不是宿主，而是家园。

2340803152.name: Balance of Power
2340803152.flavor: "In my mind I heard it whisper: 'come and see.'"
2340803152.lore:
Maya Sundaresh sits hunched over a display, the only source of light in her dark office. Brain wave scans of 16 Exos read flatline on the monitor. "How is Doctor Ardehi?" she asks into an open mic.

"Dead." Chioma Esi's voice is a hoarse whisper.

Maya switches to the security camera in Veil Containment and sees her wife kneeling on the catwalk over Doctor Ardehi's body. A procession of dead Exos are slumped over the railings to Chioma's left and right. Maya tabs away to study a bar graph.

"Neuropathy reports show a spike in activity in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus in the moments before brain death," Maya reports, eliciting a shaky sigh from Chioma over the comms before she continues her analysis. "The spikes plateaued for one fifth of a second, which may indicate a receptor error. We may need to utilize an intermediary rather than direct connections. Do the hard wires show any damage?"

Maya tabs back to the security feed, watching as Chioma wipes her eyes and then assesses one of the dead Exos, checking a thick cable plugged into the back of his head. "No sign of damage. Capacitance switches didn't trigger. It's…" She swallows down bile. "The problem isn't our hardware…"

'It's theirs,' is a whisper only Maya can hear.
 
"It's theirs," Maya agrees aloud.

"I think—I think we need to stop," Chioma finds the strength to admit. "Reassess our findings. Resume analysis of the initial electromagnetic anomaly before contact. We can't keep… we can't…"

"Keep shoveling coal into the furnace?" Maya suggests as she leans back into her chair. Chioma is too taken aback by the casual disregard to loss of life to reply. "You're right." Maya continues. "But we're not stopping. We're reorienting. The Veil is the future of humanity."

For a moment, neither woman says anything. There is only the soft hum of electronics in a darkened room to fill Maya's senses. That, and a static hiss at the back of her mind.
 
"The Veil is dangerous," Chioma asserts, her voice is tinged with a tremor of emotion.  Fear of losing the woman she loves keeps her from pushing harder as they stand on the edge of moral precipice together.

'It is.'
 
"It is," Maya agrees aloud. "We must treat it with caution, respect, and also… reverence." A thought crystallizes. "We must treat it like a knife."
2340803152.lore_zh:
玛雅·桑戴尔什蜷缩着身子坐在显示器前，这是她黑暗的办公室里唯一的光源。显示器上是16名Exo呈平线的脑电波扫描结果。“阿尔代希博士怎么样了？”她对着开放式麦克风问道。

“死了。”希欧玛·艾西的声音嘶哑而低沉。

玛雅切换到面纱遏制舱的监控摄像头，看到她妻子跪在走道上阿尔代希博士尸体前。希欧玛左右两边的栏杆上耷拉着一群死去的Exo。玛雅切换出来，转而研究一张条形图。

“神经病变报告显示，在脑死亡的前一刻，前额叶皮层和海马体的活动出现了激增，”玛雅的报告引得希欧玛在通讯器中发出一声颤抖的叹息，然后她继续分析道。“激增在五分之一秒内趋于平稳，这可能表明出现了接收器错误。我们可能需要利用媒介而不是直接连接。硬导线有损坏吗？”

玛雅轻击回到安保影像，看着希欧玛擦了擦眼睛，然后对其中一名死亡的Exo进行评估，检查他后脑勺上插着的一根粗电缆。“没有损坏迹象。电容开关没有触发。这…”她咽了一口。“问题不在于我们的硬件…”

“是他们的问题，”只有玛雅才能听到这声低语。
 
“是他们的问题，”玛雅大声表示赞同。

“我想——我想我们得停下来，”希欧玛鼓起勇气承认道。“重新评估我们的发现。继续分析接触之前的初始电磁异常。我们不能继续…我们不能…”

“继续火上浇油？”玛雅边说边靠在椅子上。这种漠视生命损失的随意态度让希欧玛惊讶得无法回答。“你说得对。”玛雅继续道。“但我们不会停下来。我们会重新适应。面纱是人类的未来。”

一时间，两个女人都没有说话。玛雅只感觉到黑暗房间里电子设备发出的轻微嗡鸣声。此外，她的脑海中还回荡着静电的嘶嘶声。
 
“面纱很危险，”希欧玛断言道，她的声音因饱含情绪而有些颤抖。此刻她们正一起立于道德的悬崖边上，而她害怕失去自己所爱的女人，不敢再多使一点劲。

“的确。”
 
“的确，”玛雅大声赞同道。“我们对待它时必须带着谨慎、尊重，还有…敬畏。”一个想法逐渐清晰起来。“就像是在对待一把匕首。”

1446374842.name: Gifted Conviction
1446374842.lore:
The H.E.L.M. is quiet save for a few robotic sentries monitoring the systems close by. The tablet in Ikora's grasp beeps in response to her touch and a set of projections appears before her. She searches through the information on the Sol Divisive—models, weaknesses, radiolaria research, even Hidden-specific analyses of their habits and types.

She glides her index finger over the screen until she finds a recording of a troop of Goblins being felled by a Guardian. It's quick—a couple of shots at most before they crumble to the ground in a puddle of radiolaria and the recording stops. The dim eye of the broken Vex catches her attention and she becomes so lost in contemplation that she barely hears another enter the room. She turns her head.

"Mithrax," Ikora acknowledges with a small nod.

"Ikora," he says, returning the greeting. "Has your research proven fruitful?"

"Sadly, no," she answers. Her gaze returns to the screen, and she sighs. "I've spent hours investigating the factions most likely to support the Witness, but it all just feels like… a distraction. Like they're fodder for its end goal."

Mithrax hums in agreement, his attention on the Vex Goblin she'd previously been transfixed by.

"Why would the Sol Divisive consider throwing themselves into the line of fire for something like the Final Shape?" she asks.

"Maybe… they simply have faith."

"Faith?" Ikora huffs involuntarily, something akin to a faintly sardonic laugh. "We know the Sol Divisive are an anomaly among the Vex, but are they even capable of that?"

"What else would convince one to commit life and death to a cause, if not faith in said cause?" Mithrax's tone is one of self-recognition, of understanding. "The idea of a better future."

A natural feeling of defiance wells up in her at the thought. She's known the underlying gnawing of expectation in words like 'perfection' and 'faith.' 1446374842.lore_zh:
除了几个监视附近星系的机器人哨兵外，应急后勤行动中心内一片寂静。艾可拉手中的平板电脑在她的触摸下哔哔作响，一组投影出现在她面前。她搜索着有关太阳系分支的信息——模型、弱点、活性放射体液研究，甚至还有针对其习性和类型的隐秘者专题分析。

她的食指在屏幕上滑动，直到她找到了一段哥布林小队被一名守护者击倒的录像。过程很快——最多也就几枪，然后他们就倒在地上，变成了一滩活性放射体液，录像随之停止。破损Vex昏暗的眼睛引起了她的注意，她沉浸在自己的沉思中，几乎没有听到另一个人走进房间。她转过头。

“米瑟拉克斯，”艾可拉微微点头致意。

“艾可拉，”他说道，回以问候。“你的研究有什么成果吗？”

“很遗憾，没有，”她的目光回到屏幕上，叹了口气。“我花了好几个小时来调查最有可能支持见证者的派系，但这都像是…障眼法。就好像他们是它最终目标的炮灰。”

米瑟拉克斯哼呜着表示同意，注意力转到了刚才引起她注意的Vex哥布林身上。

“为什么太阳系分支会愿意为了终焉之形那样的东西而吃枪子？”她问道。

“也许…他们只是有信仰而已。”

“信仰？”艾可拉不由自主地咆哮了一声，像是一种略带讥讽的嘲笑。“我们知道太阳系分支是Vex中的异类，但他们真的能拥有信仰吗？”

“如果不是信仰，还有什么能说服一个人为一项事业献身？”米瑟拉克斯的语气是一种自我认可，一种理解。“对美好未来的憧憬。”

艾可拉保持着沉默。她再次望向了那哥布林的独眼。

“他们选择自己的道路是有原因的，这给了他们使命。和我们并无不同，”米瑟拉克斯解释道，用手对着屏幕比划。“也许这就是太阳系分支认为自己可以达到完美的方式。”

艾可拉侧头思忖他的话。他的意见不无道理，这也是Vex会乐于接受的那种信仰：追求尽善尽美。一想到这里，她心里自然涌起一股抵触的情绪。她深知“完美”和“信仰”等词背后的期望带来的痛苦。这些想法驱使她走过了大半生，而在追逐这些想法的过程中，把她化作了自己的无数个版本。

艾可拉用手指在平板电脑上轻轻扫了一下，录像随之消失，取而代之的是一组新的战斗人员。

“重新评估自己的信仰永远都不晚，”她说道。

1951308312.name: Gifted Conviction
1951308312.lore:

She searches through the information on the Sol Divisive—models, weaknesses, radiolaria research, even Hidden-specific analyses of their habits and types.

She glides her index finger over the screen until she finds a recording of a troop of Goblins being felled by a Guardian. It's quick—a couple of shots at most before they crumble to the ground in a puddle of radiolaria and the recording stops. The dim eye of the broken Vex catches her attention and she becomes so lost in contemplation that she barely hears another enter the room. She turns her head.

"Mithrax," Ikora acknowledges with a small nod.

"Ikora," he says, returning the greeting. "Has your research proven fruitful?"

"Sadly, no," she answers. Her gaze returns to the screen, and she sighs. "I've spent hours investigating the factions most likely to support the Witness, but it all just feels like… a distraction. Like they're fodder for its end goal."

Mithrax hums in agreement, his attention on the Vex Goblin she'd previously been transfixed by.

"Why would the Sol Divisive consider throwing themselves into the line of fire for something like the Final Shape?" she asks.

"Maybe… they simply have faith."

"Faith?" Ikora huffs involuntarily, something akin to a faintly sardonic laugh. "We know the Sol Divisive are an anomaly among the Vex, but are they even capable of that?"

"What else would convince one to commit life and death to a cause, if not faith in said cause?" Mithrax's tone is one of self-recognition, of understanding. "The idea of a better future."

Ikora remains quiet. Her eyes find the single eye of the Goblin once more.

"They chose their path for a reason that gives them purpose. Not unlike ourselves," Mithrax elaborates, hand gesturing to the screen. "Perhaps that is how the Sol Divisive believe they can achieve perfection."

Ikora's head tilts up as she considers his words. His suggestion makes sense, and it is the sort of faith a Vex would embrace: the pursuit of total perfection. A natural feeling of defiance wells up in her at the thought. She's known the underlying gnawing of expectation in words like 'perfection' and 'faith.' The ideals that have driven her throughout most of her life, as she'd morphed into countless versions of herself in pursuit of them.

Ikora swipes her finger across the tablet and the recording disappears, replaced with a new set of combatants.

"It's never too late to re-evaluate your faith," she says.

2915174768.name: Mask of Fealty
2915174768.source: Source: Solo Expert and Master Lost Sectors
2915174768.source_zh: 来源：单人专家和大师遗失区域
2915174768.lore:
Ghar's ex-Legion. Ex-Cabal, really, if you're getting technical about it.  

But he still recognizes the tension that permeates the cargo hold: a mix of restlessness and nerves, like that of soldiers on their first real patrol.

His new Lightbearer friends aren't green recruits. They're veterans of the end-times, same as him. But he's had much longer to come to terms with his new independence.

They're still braced for the Vanguard to come crashing in here. Waiting for some eleventh-hour betrayal on his part.

But it's a brand-new world out here.

The Lightbearers brought the goods: Weapons. Artifacts. Enough to sell, and enough to see them through whatever comes next.

Ghar's got the salvaged Harvester. And Ghar's got the plans.

"All right, you dogs." Their grasp of Ulurant is abysmal, so he speaks their tongue. "You've done your service to your Vanguard. Leave war to the Hive gods, and those that feed them."

He looks down at them, his new crew. Three Human, eager faces, three metal drones. They want to see the stars. They want a little taste of the better life.

"We've got ourselves a crew of seven seasoned killers and a great big universe out there." Ghar grunts. "Let's go get rich."
2915174768.lore_zh:
加尔曾是军团成员，准确地说，曾是卡巴尔。  

但他依然能辨识货舱里弥漫的紧张气氛：混合着躁动与焦虑，就像士兵们第一次真正巡逻时的感觉。

他的新负光者朋友们并非新兵。和他一样，他们都是经历过末世的老手，只不过他有更长的时间来适应自己的独立身份。

他们仍在担心先锋会突然冲进这里，或是他会在最后关头背叛。

但外面是一个全新的世界。

负光者们带来了物资：武器、神器。足够出售变卖，也足够他们应对接下来的一切。

加尔手上有回收来的收割者，并且已有计划。

“好了，狗狗们。”他们对乌鲁兰语掌握得不好，所以他用他们的语言发话。“你们已经为先锋做出了应有的贡献，把战争留给邪魔族众神和那些喂养他们的家伙吧。”

他低头看向他的新船员：三个有着热切面孔的人类和三架金属无人机。他们渴望探索星辰，渴望品味更美好的生活。

“七个资深的杀手，面对广袤的宇宙。”加尔咕哝道。“我们一起去发财吧。”

405059572.name: Young Ahamkara's Spine
405059572.flavor: Give me your arm, oh bearer mine. Let me help you fill the world with teeth.
405059572.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
405059572.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
405059572.lore:
Bones! Let's wear some bones! 

Oh, it's a taste many Guardians develop. I think because they feel a wee bit spectral. All this transmatting leaves one saying "Am I still here? Am I flesh or am I mist?" So, you strap some old bones to your arm, bones that've been unbreakable for an eon, and you feel solid again. More yourself. 

Bearers of a particular species of bone do claim—and mind that I'm not recommending these bones—that the fossils grant them unusual powers. Nothing too wild. A little more of this and that. 

My own research suggests these special bones come from a species of draconic post-Traveler neolife called 'ahamkara'. They apparently talked—loved the phrase 'o seeker mine'—and troubled us enough to be hunted to extinction. If you wanted some more of these bones for your friends, I might know a source…
405059572.lore_zh:
骸骨！我们带些骸骨吧！

哎，守护者就喜欢这种感觉。可能因为他们觉得这样有点点怪诞吧，给人感觉“我在哪儿？这是梦境还是现实？”所以你将这些坚不可摧的远古骸骨附在手上，让自己更坚固。超越自我。

这些特殊骸骨的佩戴者声称——我可不是在推销这些骸骨啊——这些化石赋予了他们非同寻常的力量。没什么太狂野的。只是难免有些这样或那样的怪异。

我亲自研究过了，这些特殊的骨骼来自一个叫做“阿罕卡拉”的新生龙族旅行者。他们显然说过——喜欢“来追寻我的骨骼”这个词——这让我们很困惑，他们不怕被追杀灭绝吗？如果你想给你的朋友捎些骸骨，我有货源……

1803778317.name: Lucky Raspberry
1803778317.flavor:
> No one has ever died wearing me.
# It's true. She leaves the unworthy before they fall.
1803778317.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
1803778317.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
1803778317.lore:
"I dunno. Hunter just came in one day with this odd Arc-reacting circuit, asking what it might be good for. All she could tell me was she scored it off some derelict satellite that crashed in the EDZ. So I ran diagnostics on them and it ebbed and flowed with massive Arc fluctuations. No pattern, no match to known solar or extra-solar events. Just random-like. So I hooked one into an old Malina vest we had lying around, and wished her luck. Word's got out, I guess." 

—Overheard in the Tower
1803778317.lore_zh:
“我不知道。一天，猎人带着这个古怪的电弧反应电路过来，问这个可能有什么用。她只说是她在欧洲无人区坠毁的一些遗弃的卫星上取下来的。然后我诊断发现上面有大量的电弧波动流下，和已知的灼烧或超灼烧事件模式方法都不一样，都是随机的。所以我随意找了件老玛丽娜胸甲把它挂在里面，并祝她好运。反正话说出去了。”

——高塔里偷听到的

3960926757.name: Knucklehead Radar
3960926757.flavor: You can see the point, right? Who wants to team up with one?
3960926757.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
3960926757.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
3960926757.lore:
"If you were rich, what would you do with all your money?" 
"Uh… I dunno. Maybe start my own business. Be some kinda bounty hunter." 
"What you mean, bounty hunter? We got thousands of Guardians running around, bounty-hunting anything that moves!" 
"Nuh-uh! That's all just sport. Them Awoken out in the Reef, I figure they might pay me to hunt folks down. And I got a secret. It's gonna gimme a real leg up on all them Guardians who come to copycat me when they see what a good idea I got." 
"Yeah? What is it?" 
"This Hunter, she sold me a visor that lets you find all the stupid enemies in a crowd. Called it 'knucklehead radar' or something like that." 
"Huh. How's it work?" 
"Couldn't tell ya."
3960926757.lore_zh:
“你要是有钱了，会怎么花？”
“呃……我不知道。可能先创业吧，做个悬赏猎人什么的。”
“悬赏猎人是指什么？我们成千上万的守护者每天跑来跑去就是在狩猎悬赏！”
“不是啦！那只是休闲运动。那些暗礁之外的觉醒者们，我觉得他们才是会花大量跑腿费雇我狩猎的人。我有个秘密，要是让外面那些守护者知道了，肯定都堵在我家门前想要抄袭我的好主意。”
“嗯？是什么？”
“有个猎人，她卖给我了一个视觉装置，可以显示人群中所有的白痴敌人。她叫它‘傻瓜雷达'还是什么的。”
“嗯，管用吗？”
“不告诉你。”

3570710433.name: Knucklehead Radar
3570710433.flavor: You can see the point, right? Who wants to team up with one?
3570710433.lore:
"If you were rich, what would you do with all your money?" 
"Uh… I dunno. Maybe start my own business. Be some kinda bounty hunter." 
"What you mean, bounty hunter? We got thousands of Guardians running around, bounty-hunting anything that moves!" 
"Nuh-uh! That's all just sport. Them Awoken out in the Reef, I figure they might pay me to hunt folks down. And I got a secret. It's gonna gimme a real leg up on all them Guardians who come to copycat me when they see what a good idea I got." 
"Yeah? What is it?" 
"This Hunter, she sold me a visor that lets you find all the stupid enemies in a crowd. Called it 'knucklehead radar' or something like that." 
"Huh. How's it work?" 
"Couldn't tell ya."
3570710433.lore_zh:
“你要是有钱了，会怎么花？”
“呃……我不知道。可能先创业吧，做个悬赏猎人什么的。”
“悬赏猎人是指什么？我们成千上万的守护者每天跑来跑去就是在狩猎悬赏！”
“不是啦！那只是休闲运动。那些暗礁之外的觉醒者们，我觉得他们才是会花大量跑腿费雇我狩猎的人。我有个秘密，要是让外面那些守护者知道了，肯定都堵在我家门前想要抄袭我的好主意。”
“嗯？是什么？”
“有个猎人，她卖给我了一个视觉装置，可以显示人群中所有的白痴敌人。她叫它‘傻瓜雷达'还是什么的。”
“嗯，管用吗？”
“不告诉你。”

3960926756.name: Celestial Nighthawk
3960926756.flavor: Starlight is your guide. No vacuum will contain you.
3960926756.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
3960926756.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
3960926756.lore:
I'm on the ground, half inside Mav's Ward. Lucky for me, it's my head that's half in. The stars over my head are going out one at a time, but that could just be Taken goo blocking my sight. 

This giant one-eyed nightmare we woke up is real unhappy to see us. This wasn't the plan—we just came here to rob him. 

Luna's dry. The 'horn's dull. Mav's either laughing, or screaming for her life spraying lead everywhere. She's floating past Psions that won't stop splitting. STOP SPLITTING. 

We're almost out of time. We have one shot. 
So I pull out the bird and give this sucker the finger. 
One red-hot glowing finger.
3960926756.lore_zh:
我躺在地上，一半身子在马福的护盾中。幸运的是，头的那半在里面。我头顶的星星一颗接着一颗消失，但可能只是因为傀儡军团阻挡了我的视线。

我们吵醒的这个巨型独眼梦靥看到我们很不开心。这在计划外——我们只是来抢劫他的。

月球好干，角都钝了。马福不知道是在大笑，还是因为四处扫射而尖叫。她飘过不停分裂的方阵士兵。不要再分裂了。

我们快没有时间了，只剩最后一次机会了。
所以我冲着这家伙竖起了大大的中指。
红彤彤的大中指。

1611241895.name: Shinobu's Vow
1611241895.flavor: "No supplies. Armor in tatters. But the refugees had asked for help. And she had given her word." —Tale of the Six Coyotes
1611241895.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
1611241895.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
1611241895.lore:
I don't know how to write this.

I died.

Well, Shinobu died.

This is hard.

But she—I?—she must have kept this journal for a reason. So here goes.

One of the Hunters, Nadiya, told me most Guardians were dead for centuries before Ghosts find them, when all traces of their first lives are long gone. "Nadiya" is a name she chose for herself.

"Shinobu isn't your name anymore," Nadiya said.

"It could be," I said.

Then Nadiya said, "Shinobu and I were going to skip town." She told me I—Shinobu—had realized there was no stopping the Fallen. That her village, Coyote, was doomed.

"She wanted to leave this place," Nadiya said. "She didn't want to die here."

So much for that.

—Excerpt from the diary of Himura Shinobu
1611241895.lore_zh:
我不知道该怎么写下这件事。

我死了。

啊，是忍野死了。

这么写真难。

但她——我？——她肯定是出于某种原因才保留了这份日志。所以就这么写吧。

娜迪亚是一名猎人，她告诉我大部分守护者在被机灵找到之前就已经死了好几个世纪，而他们第一次生命的所有痕迹早已消失无踪。“娜迪亚”是她为自己起的名字。

她说，“你的名字已经不是忍野了。”

我答，“你可以这么叫。”

接着娜迪亚说，“我和忍野本打算逃走。”她告诉我，我——忍野——早已意识到无法阻止堕落者。她说她住的狼村注定是要毁灭的。

娜迪亚说，“她想离开这个地方。”“她不想死在这里。”

事情就是这样。

——摘自忍野绯村的日记

407148246.name: Graviton Forfeit
407148246.flavor: "Doesn't matter how good you are—you stay out there too long, you're not coming back. Not the same way you left, anyway." —Tevis
407148246.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
407148246.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
407148246.lore:
Just sit down and think about what you're doing.

A big white ball rebuilt you from nothing. Guided your civilization. Transformed you. Didn't tell you why, did it? Doubt it mentioned the omnipotent space anathema that's coming to kill you and your dog and your whole soccer club, either, but what's a little xenocide between friends?

Maybe you don't care. A gun never stops and wonders if things are more complicated. It just shoots.

It's also possible that I'm just trying to get inside your head. You're a hero with a cape and a gun and a bike. You're gonna live forever. Who's got time for doubt? Fight the "Darkness"! Yeah!

You know what I'd call "dark," in the sense of "grim," in the sense of "cosmically upsetting"? A universe full of weaponized puppets, enacting a genocidal war against the servants of a rival god.

Is this making you uncomfortable? I'm sorry. I'll be more evil. Boo. Grrr.
407148246.lore_zh:
坐下来，想一想现在的情况。

一个大白球从零将你重新构建，指引你的文明，助你转变。它没有告诉你其中的原因，对吧？我怀疑它也没有提到可憎的全能外星人会来干掉你和你的狗狗，还有你那整个足球俱乐部的事吧，这一场朋友间小小的外星屠异啊！

也许你不在乎。枪是永远不会停下来思考事情是否会变得更加复杂的。它的宿命就是射击。

还有可能我正在试图进入你的思维。你是披着斗篷，带着武器，骑着机车的英雄。你会得到永生。谁有时间去怀疑呢？对抗“暗影”！是的！

你知道我会把什么东西称作既“可怕”又会“扰乱宇宙”的“黑暗”吗？一个遍布着向敌对神灵发起灭种战争武器化傀儡的宇宙。

是这个让你感到不舒服吗？抱歉。我会说得更加邪恶。呸。咕。

3987871714.name: Sealed Ahamkara Grasps
3987871714.flavor: Plating the Ahamkara bones in silver helps to quiet the auditory hallucinations… o bearer mine.
3987871714.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
3987871714.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
3987871714.lore:
Few things can see the Light, but we are not blinded. 

The Bearer seeks the truth, but what separates truth from fiction is fragile. 

A pair of truths and a single falsehood upon the Bearer we shall impart. 

Brother, ally once more, sends his regards. 

Dreamer, awakened, the Bearer shall meet. 

Light fades, deep within the Prison.
3987871714.lore_zh:
鲜有人能看见光能，但我们并不盲目。

背负者寻求真相，但真相与虚构之间的界线脆弱无比。

我们会将真相与虚妄双双授予背负者。

手足，再次缔结的盟友，向你致意。

入梦者，已然苏醒，与背负者相会。

在深邃监牢之中，光能渐衰。

1737050140.name: Fr0st-EE5
1737050140.flavor: "Hey, if it works for computers…" —Marcus Ren
1737050140.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
1737050140.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
1737050140.lore:
"Marcus, these are incredible!"
"What did I tell you? I call these bad boys the Fr0st-EE5."
"Um, come again?"
"Just call them the Frosties."
"Whatever they're called, I love them. It felt like my entire body became supercharged while running."
"Glad you like them. I still have a couple of kinks to work out, but when that's over…"
"A couple of kinks?"
"Well sometimes—and I mean very rarely—the Energy Transfer Capacitors can overheat and explode during the user's sprint. That only happens 2% of the time or something."
"Wait, you sent me on that field test knowing this?"
"I don't see the issue here."
"I'm telling Sloane."
 "Whoa, Boaz, let's not get hasty. I'll make it up to you with some sparrow mods."
"You can't buy me off— Wait, which mods are we talking about here?"
1737050140.lore_zh:
“马库斯，它们真不可思议！”
“可不是嘛，我把这双坏小子叫冰霜-EE5。”
“呃，叫什么？”
“就叫它们小霜吧。”
“不管叫什么我都喜欢。我感觉跑起来的时候整个身体都充满了能量。”
“很高兴你喜欢它们。还有几个小毛病等着我去修复呢，等解决以后……”
“几个小毛病？”
“哎呀，就是有时候——我的意思是非常罕见的时候——导能电容会在使用者冲刺时发生过热爆炸，这种意外的发生率大概只有2%吧。”
“等下，你知道会爆炸还让我去做实地试验？”
“我觉得没什么问题嘛。”
“我要向斯隆告状。”
“哇，波资，别急啊，我给你快雀模组当补偿。”
“你可别想打发我——等等，你说的是哪种模组？”

4002939008.name: Khepri's Sting
4002939008.flavor: The wound is not deep, but you know it exists—and that is enough.
4002939008.source: Source: Exotic engrams; extremely rare world drops.
4002939008.source_zh: 来源：异域记忆水晶；极稀有世界掉落。
4002939008.lore:
The Hunter pushed off the windowsill she'd been leaning on and stretched out her arm so the metal scarab on her gauntlet flashed in the sun.

"And here I thought I was bein' subtle."

The Titan's smile widened. "You know what they say about Hunters."

"Everything you've heard about Hunters is true. Everything."

As if to underscore her point, a sizzling Line Rifle bolt sizzled through the cracked window and knocked the Titan dead.

When he came to, the Hunter was lounging on a pile of smashed and broken Vex chassis.

The Titan let out a low whistle, impressed. "Mission accomplished."

"Hm," the Hunter agreed. "On to that other mission we were discussing."

"Ah," said the Titan. "And if we're, uh, both wearing beetles?"

It was the Hunter's turn to smile, sharp and swift as a blade. "You know what else they say about Hunters. We're good at adapting."
4002939008.lore_zh:
猎人推开她一直靠着的窗台，伸出手来，她臂铠上的金属圣甲虫在阳光下闪闪发光。

“我还以为我已经够敏感了呢。”

泰坦的笑容更灿烂了。“你知道他们是怎么说猎人的。”

“你听说的关于猎人的一切都是真的。所有的一切都是。”仿佛是为了强调她的观点，一发滋滋作响的线性步枪子弹穿过打开的窗口，杀死了泰坦。

他醒来的时候，猎人已经懒洋洋地站在一堆破烂的Vex骨架上。

泰坦轻轻吹了声口哨，深受触动。“任务完成了。”

“唔，”猎人认可道，“该说说我们之前讨论的另外那个任务了。”

“啊，”泰坦答道，“要是我们，呃，都用上大槌呢？”

这回轮到猎人笑了，她的笑容就像刀刃般犀利而迅速。“你知道他们还说了猎人些什么的。我们很擅长适应。”

“唔，”猎人认可道，“该说说我们之前讨论的另外那个任务了。”

“啊，”泰坦答道，“要是我们，呃，都用上大槌呢？”

这回轮到猎人笑了，她的笑容就像刀刃般犀利而迅速。“你知道他们还说了猎人些什么的。我们很擅长适应。”

1709794165.name: Radiant Dance Machines
1709794165.flavor: Built for swift movement, they provide unexpected and decisive social benefits.
1709794165.lore:
Quick-minded Ylaia allows herself to be swept along in the plane's pulsing surge of energy.

In the space around her, Xivu Arath's Hive growl and click, tearing at the layered magics with their teeth. They can feel she is close.

She trails her fingers through the energies, making a broad ripple as she pulls toward a place she found before, when she was groping blindly for a way home.

There.

She twists in the stream and lets herself become known. Relief colors the air around her, promising the Dreaming City, Savathûn held still in stone, vulnerable for the first time in untold billions of years.

The Hive shriek in triumph, shimmering into focus as they converge on her plane.

Ylaia wraps herself in the whisper of a spell and pushes out of the Ley Line. The roaring Hive surge hungrily out of the rupture behind her… and tumble into nothing.

Dangling from a ribbon of runes, Ylaia watches their long fall onto the distant black stone of a forgotten place. The spell cuts into her hand as she pulls herself back into the stream.

She wraps the plane around herself once more, clears her mind, and waits.
1709794165.lore_zh:
思维敏捷的伊莱娅任由自己在位面的脉冲浪涌中被裹挟着前行。

在她周围的空间里，希乌阿拉斯的邪魔族咆哮着，咔嚓一声，用尖牙利齿撕扯着层层魔法。他们能感觉到她就在不远处。

她用手指在能量流中探寻着，激起巨大的涟漪，向她之前找到的地方费力移动，当时她正在盲目地摸索着回家的路。

就在那儿。

她在涌流中扭动，有意暴露自己。四周的氛围缓和了下来，显露出幽梦之城，以及在石中一动不动，数十亿年来第一次变得脆弱不堪的萨瓦图恩。

邪魔族胜利地尖叫着，聚集到她的位面上，闪烁成形。

伊莱娅将自己裹在咒语的低语中，冲出了灵脉。咆哮的邪魔族如饥似渴地从她身后的裂口中汹涌而出…然后跌进了虚无。

伊莱娅悬挂在一条符文丝带上，看着它们坠落到深远处一个被遗忘之地的黑色石头上。忍着咒语扎进手里的剧痛，她费劲地把自己拉回了涌流之中。

她再一次用位面把自己包裹起来，整理思绪，伺机而动。

94775422.name: AION Renewal Grips
94775422.flavor: "I sang him a song of the Long Drift. He did not know the words, but he understood." —Azeryks, un-Wintered
94775422.lore:
Levaszk my friend has brought us to a green world. The green of Exile, he says. Our torn capes and chipped paint were prophecy. We are meant to be here. 

Levaszk is gifted with tongues. He can convince anybody of anything, even the Humans. He sits on a carpet woven by small Human hands and sings to their Diin about local gravity and chemical reactions. Servitors listen and sing descant, calculating Ether-gain from huge pillows of slime mold.  

Our new home is warmer and wetter than Luna. The throat doesn't click so dryly against inhaled Ether. It's good, it's good—except for the fear of mold growing in rebreather linings. Except for when the wet against my shell makes my lower arms ache with Venus's memory. 

Rhys, the Human Splicer-apprentice, sings another question to me. I settle my shoulders under my cloak and gesture: apologies, again? 

"You and your people maintain ancient systems," he repeats. "How do you—" here he sings a note I do not understand. He sees my confusion. "New and old. Scrap, garbage, rusting trash. New metal. Together?" 

"We are used to building with scrap," I sing back, and we enter a discussion of material recycling. They are used to scrap-patchwork here too, on Kepler. 

Light fades from the sky, and his Splicer-master approaches. "Karrh-nahan," I say politely. She smiles with her mobile, fleshy cheeks. "Athareks," she says to me, her best attempt yet. Rhys is lucky; his name is no trouble for either of us to say. 

The Humans are not worried about blows from a stranger's hand. They come up to me, my four arms filled with stolen knives, and all they ask is the composition and tensile strength of the metal. The engine that drives them is not fear or resource-hunger, but curiosity. We are trying to learn from them, we poor Exiles. 

But they have their own ways, and it is time for their evening ritual. Carnahan urges Rhys up from his seat. 

We nod to each other, the young Splicer-apprentice and the aging Exile.  

There will be time to solve the problems of materials science later.
94775422.lore_zh:
我的朋友列瓦兹克带我们来到绿色星球。他说这是流亡之地的绿。我们破碎的披风与斑驳的漆层皆是预言。我们注定在此。 

列瓦兹克天生雄辩。他能说服任何人，哪怕是人类。他坐在人类小手编织的地毯上，向他们的迪因神吟唱局部重力与化学反应。魔眼们听着，用黏菌构成的蓬松坐垫计算乙太收益，唱起计算的和声。  

新家园比月球温暖潮湿。吸入乙太时咽喉不再干涩作响。很好，很好——除了会担心呼吸器衬里发霉。除了当湿气渗入我的甲壳时，下臂总会泛起金星的记忆性疼痛。 

瑞斯，那名人类熔岩军团学徒，又用歌声向我抛来一个问题。我裹紧斗篷下的肩膀，比了个手势：抱歉，请重复？ 

“你们族人维护着古老的系统，”他复述道，“你们怎么——”此处他唱出一个我无法理解的音符。他察觉到了我的困惑。“新旧交融。废料，垃圾，锈蚀的废弃物。崭新金属。如何共存？” 

“我们惯于用废料建造。”我以歌声回应，随即我们展开了关于材料回收的讨论。在开普勒这里，他们也擅长用废料拼凑修补。 

天光渐暗时，他的熔岩军团导师走近。“卡恩-纳罕。”我礼貌地问候。她肌肉灵活的脸颊扬起笑容。“阿萨雷克斯。”这是她迄今为止对我名字最标准的发音。瑞斯很幸运，我们双方念他的名字都不拗口。 

这些人类不畏惧陌生人的拳脚。即便我四臂环抱着偷来的刀具，他们凑近时只关心金属的成分与抗拉强度。驱动他们的不是恐惧或资源饥渴，而是纯粹的好奇。我们这些可怜的流亡氏族正试图向他们学习。 

但他们有自己的生活方式，晚间仪式时间已到。卡纳汉催促瑞斯起身。 

我们互相颔首致意，年轻的熔岩军团学徒与年迈的流亡氏族。  

材料科学的难题可以留待日后解决。

3218422834.name: AION Renewal Vest
3218422834.flavor: "I must have faith in something." —Azeryks, un-Wintered
3218422834.lore:
No Archon, no Kell, no hand on the docking blade. None of us hungrier for Ether than a Baron. This is what we said. This is what we believed. If Exile has a creed, it is this: we will not be led. 

But if Levaszk my friend tells me that we must have an Archon to make our Gift-Ether, how can I say no? 

My hatchlings, you thriving scraps of Exile, Levaszk saved your lives like he saved mine. Brought us far out of range of Dusk and the deathless monsters eating the Light of the Great Machine. Life is soft here—so fresh from the molt, a touch would bruise its shell. 

He says that this world is a gift, that we can relinquish the base Ether of Sol to breathe its presence. We will become weighty, meaningful followers of a true path. 

Is this our true path? Exiled from Riis, then from our own Houses? This I don't know. The Great Machine left us and took our true path from us, I think. I was not born to a kind fate. 

But Levaszk offers us a path.  

Look, this is my last Ether seed. This is the end of the cache I kept hidden from all of you. Look, I release the valve. See it rising purple into the air—the last breath of Ether wheedled from Luna's bare ground. 

Our Servitors could set up the light-arrays, coax what bare scraps of Ether we could get from solar power. I could breathe it and survive. But Levaszk my friend and Archon says that we can breathe the Ether of this world, heavy with dark matter, and do more than survive. 

Fated or not, there is only one path for us.
3218422834.lore_zh:
没有执政官，没有凯尔，没有放在截肢刃上的手。我们中再无人比公爵更渴求乙太。这是我们的宣言，也是我们的信仰。若流亡氏族有信条，那便是：我们不受摆布。 

可若我的朋友列瓦兹克声称必须拥立执政官来制造馈赠乙太，我怎能拒绝？ 

我的幼雏们啊，你们这些茁壮成长的流亡残渣，正如曾拯救我一般，列瓦兹克挽救了你们的性命。他带我们远离黄昏氏族的疆界，远离那些啃噬大机器光能的永生怪物。此间生命如此娇嫩——仿佛刚破茧的新生儿，轻轻一碰就会在甲壳上留下瘀痕。 

他说这个世界是份馈赠，说我们可以摒弃太阳系粗劣的乙太，呼吸此地的气息。我们将成为有分量、有意义的循路者，踏上真正的道途。 

但这真是我们的正道吗？先是从里斯流亡，再被自己的氏族抛弃？我不得而知。大机器离我们而去时，我想它已带走了我们真正的道途。我生来就不被命运眷顾。 

但列瓦兹克为我们指明前路。  

看，这是我最后的乙太籽粒。这是瞒着你们所有人私藏的库存尽头。看啊，我旋开阀门。看着紫色雾气升腾——这是从月球荒芜地表榨取的最后一缕乙太。 

我们的魔眼本可以架设光能阵列，从太阳能中提取微薄乙太。我靠它本可以勉强维生。但我的朋友兼执政官列瓦兹克说，我们能呼吸这个世界饱含暗物质的乙太，不止于苟活。 

天命与否，我们只有一条路可走。

3389206211.name: AION Renewal Cloak
3389206211.flavor: "We were hatched in the dark. Now we breathe it." —Azeryks, Herald of the Archon
3389206211.lore:
We are cut off from the Aionians, and they are cut off from the Giver. Levaszk my friend and Archon speaks law, and he has spoken this.  

But Rhys the apprentice-Splicer is my friend too. I breathe only lightly of the Gift-Ether as I make my way to the Human settlement. But I must breathe a little. It fogs my mind, I think—or is that only the worry of a weak and disrespectful Dreg? 

I know where my friend, the Splicer-apprentice, lives. His door is not locked.  

I tap at the Human-sized door. I open it, folding myself to enter. Rhys looks up from his work. He is Reviewer Three for a cousin's dissertation, he told me. It is an honor for one not yet a master himself. 

"There is something wrong," I sing to him. "The Gift-Ether has twisted Levaszk's mind. He is sick. If I tell you the symptoms, will you tell an apothecary?" 

My friend is brave. He nods to me and opens a new file on his pad. 

Is it bravery to betray Levaszk so? 

"He imagines the Giver speaks to him. He imagines himself a priest of a new god, and us his acolytes." 

Rhys beckons me to say more. My mandibles ache with muscle tension and the cold of the Gift-Ether. Some painful thing rises in my throat. 

"The Prime Archon Levaszk is the savior of his people," I say, and when I speak it is in Levaszk's voice. 

I clap a hand to my mouth to stop the voice. The edge of my rebreather slams into my jaw.  

"Azeryks, my Housemate, my trusted hand," I croon through my palm. "Are you so quickly given over to cowardice? This is our true fate. This is the path given to us. I will lead us there, our House glad, powerful, singing hymns to the Giver." 

My friend Rhys's eyes are huge in his head, so bright with fear I would have thought him breathing Ether. This is what I have given him, this fear is Exile's host-gift. 

My tongue is my own for a bare moment. "Do not trust me again," I tell Rhys. 

His door bangs loudly against its frame as I leave. 

And where else do I have left to go but back to Levaszk—my Archon, my friend?
3389206211.lore_zh:
我们与艾昂人断了联系，而他们与赐予者的纽带也被切断。我的朋友与执政官列瓦兹克以律法之言宣告了这一切。  

但熔岩军团学徒瑞斯也是我的朋友。前往人类聚居地的路上，我只敢浅尝赐礼乙太。可总得吸一点儿。这让我神志昏沉——或许只是我这个懦弱不敬的堕落者士兵在胡思乱想？ 

我知道我的朋友，熔岩军团学徒的住处。他的门没锁。  

我叩响人类尺寸的门扉，蜷身钻入。瑞斯从文献中抬头——他正在为某位表亲的学位论文担任评审三席，据他说这对非导师者而言是份殊荣。 

“出问题了，”我对他唱诵道，“赐礼乙太侵蚀了列瓦兹克的心智。他病了。要是我告知症状，你能转告药剂师吗？” 

我的朋友很勇敢。他点头应允，在他的数据板上新建了档案。 

这般背叛列瓦兹克，也算勇敢吗？ 

“他幻听见赐予者对他说话。幻想自己是新神的祭司，而我们是他麾下信徒。” 

瑞斯示意我继续。我的颚肢因肌肉紧绷和赐礼乙太的寒意而疼痛，喉间涌起苦涩之物。 

“首席执政官列瓦兹克乃族裔救主。”我开口时，发出的却是列瓦兹克的声音。 

我猛捂住嘴想截断声流，呼吸器边缘撞得下颌生疼。  

“阿泽瑞克斯啊，我的同族挚友，我信赖的臂膀，”那声音从我掌中低吟而出，“你竟如此轻易向怯懦臣服？这是我们真正的天命。这是赐予我们的道途。我将引领氏族抵达彼岸，让我们欢欣鼓舞，强盛无匹，为赐予者高唱赞歌。” 

我的朋友瑞斯双眸圆睁，眼中惊惧之强烈，简直像吸足了乙太。这就是我带给他的礼物，这份恐惧便是流亡氏族的见面礼。 

我的舌头短暂地重归自主。“别再相信我。”我对瑞斯说。 

当我离去时，他的门扉在门框上撞出惊天巨响。 

除了回去找列瓦兹克——我的执政官，我的朋友，我还能去往何处？

1021364471.name: AION Renewal Mask
1021364471.flavor: "A Devil or a King may still call herself Eliksni. In Exile, I am Fallen." —Azeryks, un-Wintered
1021364471.lore:
Listen, you awful hatchling Dregs, you whining scraps of flesh! We are Exile. Weak, argumentative, disrespectful wastes of Ether. That's what my Captain said at my final docking, and she was right.  

Still, we live. Still, we have Dreg-strength. We are cunning little thieves with cunning little knives, yes? Even here, on this wretched moon, we scrape enough Ether to keep ourselves going. Enough to grow, never. Enough to live, we have. 

What do you think the Houses will do when we descend from Luna to the blue land below and say, velask, it's been a while, we're here to join the effort? Will they give us cloaks and banners in soft new Dusk purple? Will they revoke our exile? 

You're young. Listen to Azeryks. Look at his scars. Four molts I've been through since Venus. The carapace remembers. If your Captain likes you, she docks you with a knife, clean and fast, at the joint. 

Mine used her hands. 

Go down to the Barons with four arms open, asking for a share of Ether? No. No. 

Levaszk brought me to Exile when I thought I would die. He showed me a way to live without Archon or Kell to dictate my growth, my life. Levaszk my friend took his wrist-blade and finished my docking. He trimmed away the shreds of muscle and shell where they met my body as I flinched and wept under his hands. 

All so my arms would grow back straight. Look at me now, Exile's hatchlings! Weak and contrary and alive! Breathing still! 

If Levaszk says go, Azeryks follows.
1021364471.lore_zh:
听着，你们这些可悲的堕落者士兵幼雏，这些哭哭啼啼的肉渣！我们是流亡氏族。孱弱、善辩、不敬的乙太废料。我的队长在我最后一次截肢时如是说道，她说得对。  

但我们依然活着。依然保有堕落者士兵的韧性。我们不就是群握着阴险小刀的狡诈小偷吗？即便在这该死的月球上，我们刮取的乙太也足够苟延残喘。永远不够成长，但足够生存。 

当我们从月球降临下方蔚蓝大地，说声“久违了，我们来共襄盛举”时，你觉得各大氏族会作何反应？会赐予我们崭新柔软的黄昏紫斗篷与旗帜？会撤销我们的流亡令？ 

你们太年轻了。听听阿泽瑞克斯的话。看看他的伤疤。自金星一别，我已历经四次蜕皮。甲壳记得一切。要是队长垂青于你，她会用利刃干净利落地刺入关节处来截肢。 

而我的队长，用的是双手。 

张开四臂去向公爵们乞讨乙太？不。绝不。 

当我以为将命丧黄泉时，是列瓦兹克带我来到流亡氏族。他教会我在没有执政官与凯尔的桎梏下生存。我的朋友列瓦兹克用腕刃完成了我的截肢。我在他的手下颤抖哭泣时，他削去了连接躯体的残存肌肉与甲壳。 

只为让我的新肢笔直重生。看看如今的我吧，流亡氏族的幼雏们！脆弱叛逆却依然活着！仍在呼吸！ 

若列瓦兹克说前进，阿泽瑞克斯必将追随。

938718424.name: AION Renewal Strides
938718424.flavor: "It takes an Archon to understand our fated Gifts." —Azeryks, un-Wintered
938718424.lore:
Levaszk is my Archon and my friend. Each time I hold a piece of fruit with my strong lower arms I remember what I owe him. He breathes in Gift-Ether, and he breathes out our future. 

Levaszk stands at the front of our Ketch, slime mold crawling up the hems of his cape. "The Aionians are jealous neighbors," he cries. "They will take all the gifts of this world and leave none for us." 

Clever Keelsk, sent down from Kings, looks up from the crowd. "We have shared until now," he says. "The Giver is huge, and we are few. We could claim half the planetoid and have Gift-Ether enough for our hatchlings' hatchlings." 

"It is not enough," Levaszk roars. He clicks deep in his chest. The thrum conducts hard through the metal of the Ketch, and all the young in the front row sway back, flinching. 

Levaszk paces through the crowd. He stares out into the sky, to the Giver. No Machine, yet still Great. 

"Look," says Levaszk, voice soft and persuasive. "What do our cousins have back in Sol? Eight livable planets and a warm sun. Endless territory and allies. The presence of the Great Machine. What do we want? This little green patch and the benevolence of the Giver. It's not so much. It's not more than we deserve." 

What does an Exile own apart from worn-down armor, apart from a little hoard of worthless treasures? We could own this place. This is what Levaszk offers to us in his open hands. 

And like we're jumping off the Ishtar Cliffs, we take it.
938718424.lore_zh:
列瓦兹克既是我的执政官也是我的朋友。每当我用强壮的下肢手臂握住果实时，都会铭记这份恩情。他吸入馈赠乙太，呼出我们的未来。 

列瓦兹克立于我们的双桅船首，菌丝在他的披风下摆攀爬。“艾昂人是善妒的邻居，”他高喊，“他们将掠夺这世界的所有恩赐，不留分毫给我们。” 

被王族氏族贬谪的聪明人基尔斯克从人群中抬头。“我们向来共享资源。赐予者如此庞大，而我们如此稀少。即便只占领半颗行星，也足够子子孙孙享用馈赠乙太。” 

“这远远不够。”列瓦兹克胸腔发出低沉咔响。震颤通过双桅船金属船体传导，前排幼虫都被震得踉跄后退。 

列瓦兹克踱步穿过人群，凝望天际的赐予者。虽非机器，依旧伟大。 

“瞧啊，”列瓦兹克的声音变得轻柔蛊惑，“我们在太阳系的表亲拥有什么？八颗宜居行星与温暖的恒星。无垠疆域与众多盟友。还有大机器的庇护。而我们想要什么？不过是这片小小绿洲与赐予者的垂怜。这点要求并不过分，这是我们应得的。” 

作为一名流亡氏族除了破旧铠甲和零碎废品还能拥有什么？我们可以占据此地。这就是列瓦兹克双手捧给我们的未来。 

于是我们接下了这份厚礼，如同跳下伊什塔悬崖那般决绝。

1629686472.name: AION Adapter Grips
1629686472.flavor: "I sang him a song of the Long Drift. He did not know the words, but he understood." –Azeryks, un-Wintered
1629686472.lore:
Levaszk my friend has brought us to a green world. The green of Exile, he says. Our torn capes and chipped paint were prophecy. We are meant to be here. 

Levaszk is gifted with tongues. He can convince anybody of anything, even the Humans. He sits on a carpet woven by small Human hands and sings to their Diin about local gravity and chemical reactions. Servitors listen and sing descant, calculating Ether-gain from huge pillows of slime mold.  

Our new home is warmer and wetter than Luna. The throat doesn't click so dryly against inhaled Ether. It's good, it's good—except for the fear of mold growing in rebreather linings. Except for when the wet against my shell makes my lower arms ache with Venus's memory. 

Rhys, the Human Splicer-apprentice, sings another question to me. I settle my shoulders under my cloak and gesture: apologies, again? 

"You and your people maintain ancient systems," he repeats. "How do you—" here he sings a note I do not understand. He sees my confusion. "New and old. Scrap, garbage, rusting trash. New metal. Together?" 

"We are used to building with scrap," I sing back, and we enter a discussion of material recycling. They are used to scrap-patchwork here too, on Kepler. 

Light fades from the sky, and his Splicer-master approaches. "Karrh-nahan," I say politely. She smiles with her mobile, fleshy cheeks. "Athareks," she says to me, her best attempt yet. Rhys is lucky; his name is no trouble for either of us to say. 

The Humans are not worried about blows from a stranger's hand. They come up to me, my four arms filled with stolen knives, and all they ask is the composition and tensile strength of the metal. The engine that drives them is not fear or resource-hunger, but curiosity. We are trying to learn from them, we poor Exiles. 

But they have their own ways, and it is time for their evening ritual. Carnahan urges Rhys up from his seat. 

We nod to each other, the young Splicer-apprentice and the aging Exile.  

There will be time to solve the problems of materials science later.
1629686472.lore_zh:
我的朋友列瓦兹克带我们来到绿色星球。他说这是流亡之地的绿。我们破碎的披风与斑驳的漆层皆是预言。我们注定在此。 

列瓦兹克天生雄辩。他能说服任何人，哪怕是人类。他坐在人类小手编织的地毯上，向他们的迪因神吟唱局部重力与化学反应。魔眼们听着，用黏菌构成的蓬松坐垫计算乙太收益，唱起计算的和声。  

新家园比月球温暖潮湿。吸入乙太时咽喉不再干涩作响。很好，很好——除了会担心呼吸器衬里发霉。除了当湿气渗入我的甲壳时，下臂总会泛起金星的记忆性疼痛。 

瑞斯，那名人类熔岩军团学徒，又用歌声向我抛来一个问题。我裹紧斗篷下的肩膀，比了个手势：抱歉，请重复？ 

“你们族人维护着古老的系统，”他复述道，“你们怎么——”此处他唱出一个我无法理解的音符。他察觉到了我的困惑。“新旧交融。废料，垃圾，锈蚀的废弃物。崭新金属。如何共存？” 

“我们惯于用废料建造。”我以歌声回应，随即我们展开了关于材料回收的讨论。在开普勒这里，他们也擅长用废料拼凑修补。 

天光渐暗时，他的熔岩军团导师走近。“卡恩-纳罕。”我礼貌地问候。她肌肉灵活的脸颊扬起笑容。“阿萨雷克斯。”这是她迄今为止对我名字最标准的发音。瑞斯很幸运，我们双方念他的名字都不拗口。 

这些人类不畏惧陌生人的拳脚。即便我四臂环抱着偷来的刀具，他们凑近时只关心金属的成分与抗拉强度。驱动他们的不是恐惧或资源饥渴，而是纯粹的好奇。我们这些可怜的流亡氏族正试图向他们学习。 

但他们有自己的生活方式，晚间仪式时间已到。卡纳汉催促瑞斯起身。 

我们互相颔首致意，年轻的熔岩军团学徒与年迈的流亡氏族。  

材料科学的难题可以留待日后解决。

3798581184.name: AION Adapter Vest
3798581184.flavor: "I must have faith in something." —Azeryks, un-Wintered
3798581184.lore:
No Archon, no Kell, no hand on the docking blade. None of us hungrier for Ether than a Baron. This is what we said. This is what we believed. If Exile has a creed, it is this: we will not be led. 

But if Levaszk my friend tells me that we must have an Archon to make our Gift-Ether, how can I say no? 

My hatchlings, you thriving scraps of Exile, Levaszk saved your lives like he saved mine. Brought us far out of range of Dusk and the deathless monsters eating the Light of the Great Machine. Life is soft here—so fresh from the molt, a touch would bruise its shell. 

He says that this world is a gift, that we can relinquish the base Ether of Sol to breathe its presence. We will become weighty, meaningful followers of a true path. 

Is this our true path? Exiled from Riis, then from our own Houses? This I don't know. The Great Machine left us and took our true path from us, I think. I was not born to a kind fate. 

But Levaszk offers us a path.  

Look, this is my last Ether seed. This is the end of the cache I kept hidden from all of you. Look, I release the valve. See it rising purple into the air—the last breath of Ether wheedled from Luna's bare ground. 

Our Servitors could set up the light-arrays, coax what bare scraps of Ether we could get from solar power. I could breathe it and survive. But Levaszk my friend and Archon says that we can breathe the Ether of this world, heavy with dark matter, and do more than survive. 

Fated or not, there is only one path for us.
3798581184.lore_zh:
没有执政官，没有凯尔，没有放在截肢刃上的手。我们中再无人比公爵更渴求乙太。这是我们的宣言，也是我们的信仰。若流亡氏族有信条，那便是：我们不受摆布。 

可若我的朋友列瓦兹克声称必须拥立执政官来制造馈赠乙太，我怎能拒绝？ 

我的幼雏们啊，你们这些茁壮成长的流亡残渣，正如曾拯救我一般，列瓦兹克挽救了你们的性命。他带我们远离黄昏氏族的疆界，远离那些啃噬大机器光能的永生怪物。此间生命如此娇嫩——仿佛刚破茧的新生儿，轻轻一碰就会在甲壳上留下瘀痕。 

他说这个世界是份馈赠，说我们可以摒弃太阳系粗劣的乙太，呼吸此地的气息。我们将成为有分量、有意义的循路者，踏上真正的道途。 

但这真是我们的正道吗？先是从里斯流亡，再被自己的氏族抛弃？我不得而知。大机器离我们而去时，我想它已带走了我们真正的道途。我生来就不被命运眷顾。 

但列瓦兹克为我们指明前路。  

看，这是我最后的乙太籽粒。这是瞒着你们所有人私藏的库存尽头。看啊，我旋开阀门。看着紫色雾气升腾——这是从月球荒芜地表榨取的最后一缕乙太。 

我们的魔眼本可以架设光能阵列，从太阳能中提取微薄乙太。我靠它本可以勉强维生。但我的朋友兼执政官列瓦兹克说，我们能呼吸这个世界饱含暗物质的乙太，不止于苟活。 

天命与否，我们只有一条路可走。

2725736573.name: AION Adapter Cloak
2725736573.flavor: "We were hatched in the dark. Now we breathe it." –Azeryks, Herald of the Archon
2725736573.lore:
We are cut off from the Aionians, and they are cut off from the Giver. Levaszk my friend and Archon speaks law, and he has spoken this.  

But Rhys the apprentice-Splicer is my friend too. I breathe only lightly of the Gift-Ether as I make my way to the Human settlement. But I must breathe a little. It fogs my mind, I think—or is that only the worry of a weak and disrespectful Dreg? 

I know where my friend, the Splicer-apprentice, lives. His door is not locked.  

I tap at the Human-sized door. I open it, folding myself to enter. Rhys looks up from his work. He is Reviewer Three for a cousin's dissertation, he told me. It is an honor for one not yet a master himself. 

"There is something wrong," I sing to him. "The Gift-Ether has twisted Levaszk's mind. He is sick. If I tell you the symptoms, will you tell an apothecary?" 

My friend is brave. He nods to me and opens a new file on his pad. 

Is it bravery to betray Levaszk so? 

"He imagines the Giver speaks to him. He imagines himself a priest of a new god, and us his acolytes." 

Rhys beckons me to say more. My mandibles ache with muscle tension and the cold of the Gift-Ether. Some painful thing rises in my throat. 

"The Prime Archon Levaszk is the savior of his people," I say, and when I speak it is in Levaszk's voice. 

I clap a hand to my mouth to stop the voice. The edge of my rebreather slams into my jaw.  

"Azeryks, my Housemate, my trusted hand," I croon through my palm. "Are you so quickly given over to cowardice? This is our true fate. This is the path given to us. I will lead us there, our House glad, powerful, singing hymns to the Giver." 

My friend Rhys's eyes are huge in his head, so bright with fear I would have thought him breathing Ether. This is what I have given him, this fear is Exile's host-gift. 

My tongue is my own for a bare moment. "Do not trust me again," I tell Rhys. 

His door bangs loudly against its frame as I leave. 

And where else do I have left to go but back to Levaszk—my Archon, my friend?
2725736573.lore_zh:
我们与艾昂人断了联系，而他们与赐予者的纽带也被切断。我的朋友与执政官列瓦兹克以律法之言宣告了这一切。  

但熔岩军团学徒瑞斯也是我的朋友。前往人类聚居地的路上，我只敢浅尝赐礼乙太。可总得吸一点儿。这让我神志昏沉——或许只是我这个懦弱不敬的堕落者士兵在胡思乱想？ 

我知道我的朋友，熔岩军团学徒的住处。他的门没锁。  

我叩响人类尺寸的门扉，蜷身钻入。瑞斯从文献中抬头——他正在为某位表亲的学位论文担任评审三席，据他说这对非导师者而言是份殊荣。 

“出问题了，”我对他唱诵道，“赐礼乙太侵蚀了列瓦兹克的心智。他病了。要是我告知症状，你能转告药剂师吗？” 

我的朋友很勇敢。他点头应允，在他的数据板上新建了档案。 

这般背叛列瓦兹克，也算勇敢吗？ 

“他幻听见赐予者对他说话。幻想自己是新神的祭司，而我们是他麾下信徒。” 

瑞斯示意我继续。我的颚肢因肌肉紧绷和赐礼乙太的寒意而疼痛，喉间涌起苦涩之物。 

“首席执政官列瓦兹克乃族裔救主。”我开口时，发出的却是列瓦兹克的声音。 

我猛捂住嘴想截断声流，呼吸器边缘撞得下颌生疼。  

“阿泽瑞克斯啊，我的同族挚友，我信赖的臂膀，”那声音从我掌中低吟而出，“你竟如此轻易向怯懦臣服？这是我们真正的天命。这是赐予我们的道途。我将引领氏族抵达彼岸，让我们欢欣鼓舞，强盛无匹，为赐予者高唱赞歌。” 

我的朋友瑞斯双眸圆睁，眼中惊惧之强烈，简直像吸足了乙太。这就是我带给他的礼物，这份恐惧便是流亡氏族的见面礼。 

我的舌头短暂地重归自主。“别再相信我。”我对瑞斯说。 

当我离去时，他的门扉在门框上撞出惊天巨响。 

除了回去找列瓦兹克——我的执政官，我的朋友，我还能去往何处？

3013134961.name: AION Adapter Mask
3013134961.flavor: "A Devil or a King may still call herself Eliksni. In Exile, I am Fallen." –Azeryks, un-Wintered
3013134961.lore:
Listen, you awful hatchling Dregs, you whining scraps of flesh! We are Exile. Weak, argumentative, disrespectful wastes of Ether. That's what my Captain said at my final docking, and she was right.  

Still, we live. Still, we have Dreg-strength. We are cunning little thieves with cunning little knives, yes? Even here, on this wretched moon, we scrape enough Ether to keep ourselves going. Enough to grow, never. Enough to live, we have. 

What do you think the Houses will do when we descend from Luna to the blue land below and say, velask, it's been a while, we're here to join the effort? Will they give us cloaks and banners in soft new Dusk purple? Will they revoke our exile? 

You're young. Listen to Azeryks. Look at his scars. Four molts I've been through since Venus. The carapace remembers. If your Captain likes you, she docks you with a knife, clean and fast, at the joint. 

Mine used her hands. 

Go down to the Barons with four arms open, asking for a share of Ether? No. No. 

Levaszk brought me to Exile when I thought I would die. He showed me a way to live without Archon or Kell to dictate my growth, my life. Levaszk my friend took his wrist-blade and finished my docking. He trimmed away the shreds of muscle and shell where they met my body as I flinched and wept under his hands. 

All so my arms would grow back straight. Look at me now, Exile's hatchlings! Weak and contrary and alive! Breathing still! 

If Levaszk says go, Azeryks follows.
3013134961.lore_zh:
听着，你们这些可悲的堕落者士兵幼雏，这些哭哭啼啼的肉渣！我们是流亡氏族。孱弱、善辩、不敬的乙太废料。我的队长在我最后一次截肢时如是说道，她说得对。  

但我们依然活着。依然保有堕落者士兵的韧性。我们不就是群握着阴险小刀的狡诈小偷吗？即便在这该死的月球上，我们刮取的乙太也足够苟延残喘。永远不够成长，但足够生存。 

当我们从月球降临下方蔚蓝大地，说声“久违了，我们来共襄盛举”时，你觉得各大氏族会作何反应？会赐予我们崭新柔软的黄昏紫斗篷与旗帜？会撤销我们的流亡令？ 

你们太年轻了。听听阿泽瑞克斯的话。看看他的伤疤。自金星一别，我已历经四次蜕皮。甲壳记得一切。要是队长垂青于你，她会用利刃干净利落地刺入关节处来截肢。 

而我的队长，用的是双手。 

张开四臂去向公爵们乞讨乙太？不。绝不。 

当我以为将命丧黄泉时，是列瓦兹克带我来到流亡氏族。他教会我在没有执政官与凯尔的桎梏下生存。我的朋友列瓦兹克用腕刃完成了我的截肢。我在他的手下颤抖哭泣时，他削去了连接躯体的残存肌肉与甲壳。 

只为让我的新肢笔直重生。看看如今的我吧，流亡氏族的幼雏们！脆弱叛逆却依然活着！仍在呼吸！ 

若列瓦兹克说前进，阿泽瑞克斯必将追随。

2306671522.name: AION Adapter Strides
2306671522.flavor: "It takes an Archon to understand our fated Gifts." –Azeryks, un-Wintered
2306671522.lore:
Levaszk is my Archon and my friend. Each time I hold a piece of fruit with my strong lower arms I remember what I owe him. He breathes in Gift-Ether, and he breathes out our future. 

Levaszk stands at the front of our Ketch, slime mold crawling up the hems of his cape. "The Aionians are jealous neighbors," he cries. "They will take all the gifts of this world and leave none for us." 

Clever Keelsk, sent down from Kings, looks up from the crowd. "We have shared until now," he says. "The Giver is huge, and we are few. We could claim half the planetoid and have Gift-Ether enough for our hatchlings' hatchlings." 

"It is not enough," Levaszk roars. He clicks deep in his chest. The thrum conducts hard through the metal of the Ketch, and all the young in the front row sway back, flinching. 

Levaszk paces through the crowd. He stares out into the sky, to the Giver. No Machine, yet still Great. 

"Look," says Levaszk, voice soft and persuasive. "What do our cousins have back in Sol? Eight livable planets and a warm sun. Endless territory and allies. The presence of the Great Machine. What do we want? This little green patch and the benevolence of the Giver. It's not so much. It's not more than we deserve." 

What does an Exile own apart from worn-down armor, apart from a little hoard of worthless treasures? We could own this place. This is what Levaszk offers to us in his open hands. 

And like we're jumping off the Ishtar Cliffs, we take it.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM—UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT 

TO: DEFENSE SECRETARY CALLAWAY 

FROM: DIRECTOR MOFFAT 

DATE: ████████ 

SUBJECT: DIABLERETS RESPONSE REPORT 

Between the hours of 19:00 and 20:00 local time, night skiers in the Vaud Alps reported a █████████  ██ that █████████ an Emerald-727 █████ ██████ into the backside of Les Diablerets. The Swiss Armed Forces were able to evacuate the mountain and secure the area while our contact notified Central of the incident. 

Upon notification of the distress call, Central concluded ███████ were unnecessary and mobilized Operation █████. Response team was activated. Primary hospitality core included: linguist █████████████, sociologist ██████████, physician ██████████, and myself.  

We were all on our own. I could tell the others were wary. Snow was deep, and we could see fires from the █████ burning in the trees. Approach of the █████ made it clear there were no █████████. Per █████ protocol, we approached without backup and read the ███████████████████████ alongside accompanying musical stimuli, then approached what we suspected was the ████. The █████ had torn a ████ through the ████, which revealed ████████████████. 

The ███████ themselves were imposing, burly,███████ structure ████████ at the top, with █████████ in a triangular █████████ and tough, thick █████. ██████ are clearly ████████, confirming our foundational hypothesis. The ██████ are being ██████ at our █████████████████. 

Aboard the █████, we also uncovered a ██████████ inside a █████████████. Stored within the █████ was a payload of ███████████████ that further research suggests was ███-engineered to consume a █████████ threat.

█████████████ confirms to me that in addition to the ████ material found in the laboratory, there is text from an additional ████████████████████████. He has begun pattern identification. Output to follow. 

Inform Pentagon their investment is seeing return. Next time company knocks, we'll put the kettle on.
2867399974.lore_zh:
美国政府内部备忘录 

收件人：国防部长卡拉韦 

发件人：莫法特主任 

日期：████████ 

主题：迪亚布勒雷山行动报告 

当地时间19:00至20:00，沃州阿尔卑斯山区夜滑者报告一场█████████  ██， █████████一架翡翠-727航班█████ ██████于迪亚布勒雷山背坡。瑞士军队完成山区疏散及封锁后，我方联络员向中央通报事件。 

在接到求救信号后，中央研判后认定无需███████ ，即刻启动“█████行动”。应急小组立即完成部署。核心接待团队包括：语言学家█████████████、社会学家██████████、医师██████████及本人。  

我们只能靠自己。看得出大家都小心翼翼的。积雪没膝，林间█████燃烧的火光清晰可辨。随着█████逼近，确认无█████████存活。依据█████协议，我们在无后援情况下向前推进，诵读着███████████████████████并辅以音乐刺激，随后接近疑似████的物体。█████撕开一道贯穿████的████，暴露出████████████████。 

███████本体魁伟骇人，███████ 结构的顶端████████，呈三角█████████排列的█████████与粗厚█████格外醒目。██████确系████████，验证了我们的基础假说。当前██████正于我们的█████████████████接受██████。 

在█████内部，我们还发现置于█████████████中的██████████。 █████内封存的███████████████经研究推测为███特制，用于吞噬█████████级威胁。

█████████████向我确认，除实验室发现的████物质外，另有源自另一份████████████████████████的文本资料。他已着手模式识别，分析结果将后续呈报。 

请转告五角大楼，他们的投资已见成效。下次贵客临门，我们自当备茶相迎。

2439379860.name: Phoenix Cradle
2439379860.flavor: For some, a nest. For the rest, a crucible.
2439379860.lore:
"Magistrate? Aodh? I'm here. I've returned."

"I know that voice. Ouros. You found the Forge."

"Yes, Magistrate."

"I knew you would. Come. Sit by me. Let us rekindle our friendship."

"…Magistrate? What happened?"

"I am Empyreal Magistrate no longer. I have not been for many years. I lost my Ghost, and so… my Light. With it went the Forge."

"But, Magistrate—"

"No. No, that title belongs to another now. You must seek them out. Gather the other Sunbreakers, and choose a new Magistrate. The Order has lacked leadership for too long. Bring them together, Ouros.

"Heat is a force that breaks bonds, shatters structure, separates elements. Heat liquefies solids, and in turn transforms them to aether. In this way, it is a force of chaos and destruction. It even tears the universe apart. In a way, it tore apart our Order."

"What do you mean?"

"The fire that burns within you—that rage, that wrath—it explodes outward upon foes. Incinerates. Destroys. But that is not all. What happens when you burn yourself or your friends?"

"Burn myself or…? The ring of flames. In it, my enemies burn, and yet my allies can walk through that fire, untouched."

"Yes! But for you it is more. Is it not so?"

"Yes. I feel stronger inside the circle."

"Exactly. But the grace of Solar Light was never meant to be ours alone. In the beginning, Sunbreakers could share the warmth of the fire within. Friends that walked in the circle felt that warmth too."

"What happened?"

"The ring of flames was a judge, granting only weal or woe. Too many who carried the Light were burned by the heat of the fire. That was part of why we Sunbreakers could not abide so-called civilization.

"Leaving wasn't easy. Not all in the Order thought it the right path. Despite the good we could do in the wilds, there was disagreement, judgement. More bonds broken than made.

"Little by little, we all lost something. Sharing the warmth of our fires with others just became… too hard. The method became a secret, and the secret became a mystery.

"Find the others. Choose an Empyreal Magistrate. Find a way to share your fire. I am too old and have no fire left to share."

"No, Aodh. Your shoulder warms mine, too. Your words kindle a new fire in me. We'll spread the flames together. And we'll find a way share the warmth again."

"But I am too old. I am blind. I have no Light."

"You've seen more than me, and your vision is so clear, it opened my eyes. You are not shadowed by a Ghost, but you're as bright as the Sun."

"For one who says so little, you have a fine way with words. Perhaps we won't have to go too far to find a new Empyreal Magistrate."
2439379860.lore_zh:
“法官？奥德？我来了。我回来了。”

“我知道这个声音。奥罗丝。你找到锻炉了。”

“是的，法官。”

“我就知道你能找到。来，坐我这。让我们来重燃我们之间的友谊。”

“……法官？发生了什么事？”

“我不再是炎阳天空法官了。已经很多年了。我失去了我的机灵，还有我的……光能。随之而去的还有锻炉。”

“但是法官——”

“不，这个头衔已经不再属于我。你必须找出他们。把其他的炎阳聚集起来，选出一个新法官。结社缺少领导的状态已经持续太久了。把他们重新凝聚起来，奥罗丝。”

“热是一种力量，能破坏联结、粉碎结构、分离元素。热量能够将固体液化，然后将其转化为以太。以这种方式而言，热量是混乱与毁灭的力量。甚至能够撕裂宇宙。某种意义上来说，也撕裂了我们的结社。”

“为什么这么说？”

“你内心燃烧的火焰——那种怒火，愤怒——向外爆发后，落在你的对手身上。点燃。毁灭。但这还不是全部。当你焚烧自己或者你的朋友后，发生了什么？”

“焚烧我自己或……？烈焰之环。在里面，我的敌人会被焚烧，我的盟友可以毫发无伤穿过烈焰。”

“是的！但对你而言，不止如此。是这样吗？”

“是的。在圆环内我感觉变强了。”

“没错。但烈日之光的恩赐从来都不仅只属于我们。在最初，炎阳可以在内部分享火焰的温暖。走进圆环内的朋友也能感觉到那种温暖。”

“发生了什么事？”

“烈焰之环曾经是一种论断，只能断祸福。太多携带光能的人被烈焰所焚烧。那只是我们炎阳无法忍受所谓“文明”的原因之一。

“离开真的很不容易。结社里并非所有人都认为这是正确的道路。尽管我们可以在野外做得很好，但仍有分歧和审判。断开的联结比重建的更多。

“一点点的，所有人都失去了某些东西。和其他人分享我们烈焰的温度这件事……太难了。方法成为秘密，秘密成为了传说。

“找到其他人。选择一个炎阳天空法官。找到分享你的烈焰的方法。我已经太老，没有火焰可以分享了。”

“不，奥德。你的肩膀也温暖着我。你的话在我心里点燃了新的火焰。我们会一起把这烈焰散播开来。我们会找到办法，再次分享温暖。”

“但我已经太老了。我瞎了，我没有光了。”

“你看得比我更多，你的眼界如此清澈，你让我打开了双眼。你没有被机灵所遮蔽，但你和太阳一样明亮。”

“对于一个话如此之少的人而言，你的言语能力极佳。也许新的炎阳天空法官远在天边近在眼前。”
